title: Issue Editorial Masthead
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Versatile Interfacial
Engineering of Core–Shell
Mesoporous Nanomaterials: Programmable Assembly, Functional Integration,
and Diverse Applications
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Integrating diverse building blocks into functional materials with tailored architectures and properties has emerged as an efficient strategy to address the demands of multifunctional applications, and core–shell mesoporous materials (CSMMs) enable the modular integration of functional components and the structural optimization of mass transfer. Enabled by multi-interface nanoassembly strategies, diverse CSMMs have been engineered and sparked intense interdisciplinary interest owing to their distinctive features, including multicomponent synergistic effects, interfacial coupling effects, and rationally designed heterogeneous architectures. Herein, this review systematically introduces the concept of “micellar coating chemistry” and summarizes current assembly strategies for the tailored synthesis of CSMMs. The rational design of structure (e.g. surface roughness, cavity, pore size, and porosity) and composition (e.g. magnetic-, noble metal-, silica-, polymer-, and carbon-based components) are highlighted. Furthermore, functionality integration (e.g. nanoparticle loading, hybridization, and surface functionalization) is also evaluated and summarized, and the diverse applications of these materials in hot fields, such as catalysis, gas sensing, environmental remediation, biomedicine, energy storage and conversion, are critically assessed and compared. This review outlines future research opportunities and challenges, and establishes a conceptual foundation for the rational design, scalable synthesis, and versatile interdisciplinary applications of CSMMs.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Ion
Accessibility Governs Electrochemically Effective
Actuation in Carbon Nanotube Muscles
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Electrochemical muscles convert charge-induced changes in conductive networks into macroscopic deformation, but stored charge does not necessarily produce mechanically effective actuation. Here, we identify spatial ion accessibility within hierarchical carbon nanotube (CNT) networks as a controlling factor in this electrochemical-mechanical coupling. We construct a solvent-tunable platform using EMIm·BF4 dissolved in propylene carbonate (PC), trimethyl phosphate (TMP), and their mixtures while retaining the same ionic species and CNT architecture. Although charge storage decreases in TMP-rich electrolytes, this change is far smaller than the more than 20-fold reduction in contraction, from 50.4% in PC to 2.1% in TMP at 2.5 V. Charge-normalized analysis shows that stored charge alone cannot predict mechanical output. In-situ Raman spectroscopy and depth-resolved TOF-SIMS and XPS analyses indicate that PC is associated with spatially extended ion access and electrochemical doping, whereas TMP predominantly supports surface-accessible charge storage. Molecular simulations further associate this contrast with differences in ion–solvent stabilization and solvation-shell reorganization. These findings establish spatial ion accessibility as a design principle for converting electrochemical charge into mechanical work in porous conductive networks.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Highly
Interconnected Cellulose Acetate Ultrafiltration
Membranes via Interfacial Hydration-Induced Phase Separation for Ultrafast
Water Purification
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Ultrafiltration is essential for ensuring water security, yet commercial ultrafiltration membranes remain constrained by the permeability-selectivity trade-off. While extensive research has focused on designing the selective skin layer, such improvements in permeance have neared a bottleneck due to the often-overlooked hydraulic resistance arising from the underlying sponge-like layer. Here, we propose a generalizable interfacial hydration-induced phase separation strategy to reconstruct the internal transport channels within the sponge-like layer of biodegradable cellulose acetate (CA) ultrafiltration membranes, enhancing permeance without sacrificing selectivity. Specifically, highly polar nanoclusters (TCZ), formed in situ via multidentate coordination between tannic acid-modified cellulose nanocrystals (TC) and Zr4+ ions, preferentially anchor within the sponge-like layer through strong interfacial interactions with the CA matrix. Acting as localized hydration seeds, these nanoclusters attract and enrich water molecules to establish water-rich microenvironments through strong hydrogen-bonding interactions, promoting local liquid–liquid demixing and driving the formation of highly interconnected, low-tortuosity water-transport pathways throughout the sponge-like layer. The resulting CTCZ membranes exhibit high water permeance (752.29 L m–2 h–1 bar–1), representing a 10-fold increase over the CA membrane, with high rejection (&gt;96%) for typical water contaminants. Notably, this strategy can also be extended to mainstream polyvinylidene fluoride and poly(ether sulfone) matrices, yielding 13-fold and 21-fold permeance enhancements, respectively. Large-area NW-CTCZ membranes fabricated via a roll-to-roll process demonstrate reliable long-term stability in surface water purification. Furthermore, life-cycle and economic analyses confirm that the CTCZ membranes, as eco-friendly and cost-effective candidates, offer a scalable and sustainable approach for water treatment.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Multifunctional
2D Polymeric Nanofiber Networks via
Proton-Mediated Assembly for High-Temperature Applications
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Advanced heat-resistant nanofibrous networks are attracting growing attention as critical functional components owing to thermostable porous architectures and selective sieving capabilities that offer reliable safeguards and a technical foundation to ensure safe operation and sophisticated manufacturing in harsh thermal environments. However, the high glass transition temperature and narrow processing window of heat-resistant polymers limit processing accuracy, making it difficult to achieve nanoscale processing of fibers and regulation of their assembled architectures, thereby causing a conflict between the heat resistance advantage and structural functionalization. Here, we report a universal proton-mediated intermolecular interaction regulation strategy for regulating the self-assembly pathway and morphology of heat-resistant nanofibers without dependence on melting or dissolution, to fabricate two-dimensional (2D) thermally reliable nanofiber networks (TR-nets) with fine separation function. By customizing the nanofiber dispersion properties and electrospraying process parameters, we couple the assembly of nanofibers mediated by proton transfer with the 2D deformation of nanofiber dispersion microdroplets sprayed from a Taylor cone, thereby manipulating the dominant intermolecular interactions to dynamically switch between repulsion and attraction in the 2D plane, regulating the topological assembly behavior of nanofiber building blocks. Benefiting from the hydrophobic porous Steiner network architecture and intrinsic material thermal stability, the fabricated TR-nets exhibit multifunctionality combining liquid repellency, air permeability, dust prevention, and sound transmission, and can withstand high-temperature environments up to 400 °C. This work may afford innovative perspectives for the advanced design and development of functionally integrated devices capable of working in high-temperature environments.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Tuning
Surface Transformations in Cobalt-Based Spinel
Oxides for Enhanced Activity and Stability in the Oxygen Evolution
Reaction
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Achieving efficient hydrogen production via water electrolysis requires the development of low-cost, highly active, and stable oxygen evolution reaction (OER) electrocatalysts. However, the OER electrocatalyst surface is not static; instead, it reconstructs and transforms dynamically and continuously during the OER. Multiple elementary processes occur simultaneously, and the OER electrocatalyst surface changes substantially as the OER proceeds. Thus, understanding these elementary processes and how they affect electrocatalytic performance is essential for OER electrocatalyst design. In this study, we demonstrate that vanadium substitution markedly enhances the OER performance of cobalt spinel oxide. Co2VO4 nanoparticles achieve a low overpotential of approximately 306 mV at 10 mA cm–2 and maintain their activity for over 80 h of chronopotentiometry measurements, significantly outperforming the lower-substituted Co2.75V0.25O4 and Co3O4. Using a multimodal characterization approach, we reveal that the enhanced activity and electrochemical stability of Co2VO4 originate from the in situ formation of hydrated and defective γ-type (Co0.75V0.25)OOH clusters that are possibly continuously self-healed through highly reversible CoII(OH)2 ↔ γ-type oxyhydroxide transformation. This reversible transformation is triggered by pronounced vanadium dissolution due to severe lattice distortion induced by tetrahedrally coordinated vanadium (+5) sites in Co2VO4. In contrast, Co2.75V0.25O4 forms an epitaxial, less hydrated β-type (Co0.92V0.08)OOH layer that degrades via vanadium leaching, causing poor stability. Overall, our findings reveal that a pronounced vanadium (+5) content in Co-based spinel facilitates the highly reversible CoII(OH) 2 ↔ γ-type oxyhydroxide transformation, which is an effective strategy to promote OER activity and stability of cobalt-based spinel oxide catalysts toward OER.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Highly Efficient
Molecular-to-Lattice Chirality Transfer
in Benzene-Based Dion–Jacobson Perovskites for Circularly Polarized
Light Detection
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Chiral organic–inorganic hybrid perovskites are emerging as promising materials for direct detection of circularly polarized light (CPL), yet their performance has remained limited by inefficient chirality transfer and weak interlayer coupling inherent in conventional Ruddlesden–Popper (RP) architectures. In this work, we report benzene-based chiral Dion–Jacobson perovskites based on chiral 1,4-bis(1-aminoethyl)benzene (BDJ)-derived diammonium spacers, which enable highly efficient molecular-to-lattice chirality transfer. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals asymmetric yet deeply penetrating hydrogen-bonding networks, accompanied by pronounced octahedral distortion and strong asymmetry in the Pb–I–Pb angles within the inorganic framework. Consistent with these distinct structural characteristics, BDJ perovskite thin films exhibit exceptionally large circular dichroism with absorption dissymmetry factors (gCD) reaching 0.014. Relative to conventional methylbenzylamine (MBA)-based RP analogues, the BDJ system shows enhanced chiroptical activity as well as a more uniform surface Pb chemical environment. Device-level studies further demonstrate rapid, bias-free CPL-responsive photodiodes exhibiting submillisecond response times and gIph values of 0.12, together with scalable photodetector arrays showing uniform handedness-selective photoresponse and CPL-dependent spatial imaging. These findings highlight chiral BDJ-based perovskites as an effective material platform for circular polarization-sensitive optoelectronics and provide design guidelines for high-performance chiral hybrid perovskites.</jats:p>

title: N‐Heterocyclic Molecular Additives Enable Solvation and Interfacial Chemistry Regulation for High‐Stability, High‐Rate, and High‐Capacity Lithium Metal Anodes
content:
An N‐heterocyclic molecule (i.e., TPTC) is demonstrated as a versatile electrolyte additive to modulate solvation and interfacial chemistry for stable Li anodes. Electron‐rich N atoms in TPTC serve as ion‐dipole sites to weaken Li+ solvation, while electron‐deficient C–H in pyridine units weakly interacts with TFSI− to generate an anion‐rich interfacial region, which generates an inorganic‐rich SEI, favoring uniform Li deposition.








ABSTRACT
Most electrolyte additives enable long‐term Li plating/stripping at <3 mA cm−2, non‐applicable to practical Li‐metal batteries (LMBs) operating at ≥5 mA cm−2 and ≥ 5 mAh cm−2. Here, we report an interaction chemistry that enables simultaneous solvation and interfacial regulation by exploring a novel N‐heterocyclic molecule (i.e., TPTC)—comprising an N‐heterocyclic core and four pyridine units–as an efficient additive for achieving ultra‐stable Li‐metal anodes under practical conditions. Electron‐rich N atoms in TPTC serve as ion‐dipole interaction sites, inducing competitive coordination that weakens Li+ solvation and enhances Li+ migration in the bulk electrolyte, which homogenizes Li+ concentration near the interface, favoring high‐rate Li deposition. TPTC also adsorbs on Li surface to construct a protective layer with a low interfacial de‐solvation barrier, which–together with low‐barrier Li+ transport through heterocyclic cavities–facilitates uniform Li deposition. Meanwhile, electron‐deficient C–H sites in pyridine weakly interact with TFSI−, forming an anion‐rich interfacial region that in situ decomposes into an inorganic‐rich interphase, affording high‐flux Li+ transport. This synergy allows stable Li plating/stripping at 10 mA cm−2/10 mAh cm−2 for 3000 h. Paired with a high‐loading LiFePO4 cathode (∼15 mg cm−2) and thin Li (∼100 µm), the cell maintains 87.8% capacity after 400 cycles.

title: Surpassing Metal‐Centric E‐Waste Recycling: Unveiling Graphite in Spent Lithium‐Ion Batteries Towards Electrocatalytic Upcycling
content:
Anodic graphite in black masses (BM) has found potential for the water oxidation reaction, validated in NMC, LFP, and LCO BM. Interestingly, graphite in BM complemented their impurity flaws toward OER via bioleaching, thermal, and mechanochemical modified pathways. Streamlined life‐cycle and techno‐economic assessments reveal the CO2‐eq emissions, economic trade‐offs, and broader sustainability implications inherent to these circular pathways.








ABSTRACT
With tonnes of battery shredded globally, tracing down pathways in upcycling black mass (BM) as catalysts would be a game changer. Existing unwavering synergic combination of inherent metals and graphite in BM drives this novel objective. Herein, we report the critical role of spent graphite for electrocatalytic water splitting applications by systematic evaluation of diverse NMC, LFP, and LCO BM. The study revealed an interesting pattern, wherein the graphite in BM complemented their impurity flaws by delivering an excellent oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity. Defects, surface activation, structural variation, and metal‐graphite synergism arising from prolonged cycle life served as a serendipitous finding of upcycling BM for OER, despite being loaded with impurities and/or degradation byproducts. Further, among these BM sets, direct upcycling of select graphite‐containing BM via mechanochemical functionalisation aided downsized derivatives delivering an overpotential of 260 mV at 10 mA cm−2, while functionalized graphite via bioleaching BM recorded an overpotential of 249 mV, an epoch‐making record in graphite upcycling. By correlating the overall insights using advanced material, electrochemical characterisation studies, and life cycle analysis, the current study unlocks spent graphite benefits for achieving sustainable energy solutions and beyond.

title: Decoupled Dual‐Stream Seawater Electrolysis Toward Cost‐Effective Green Hydrogen Production
content:
A decoupled dual‐stream seawater electrolysis strategy is proposed for cost‐effective hydrogen production. Seawater is treated into fresh seawater and ion‐enriched concentrated seawater via desalination. H2 is produced via effective fresh seawater electrolysis. The concentrated seawater is processed into electrolysis device to obtain H2 with valuable by‐products. This strategy offers a new approach for cost‐effective green hydrogen production with comprehensive seawater valorization.








ABSTRACT
Ocean, as a vast natural reservoir of ionic minerals, provides a promising approach to offset the high cost of hydrogen production from electrocatalytic water splitting. However, the complex ionic environment of seawater compels us to separate out scaling‐prone ions via cost‐effective membrane separation technology, and further separately electrolyze diluted and concentrated seawater to produce H2 and high value‐added marine chemical products. We herein apply electrodialysis to separate out divalent cations and produce twofold concentrated seawater and fresh seawater. A decoupled dual‐stream seawater electrolysis (DDSE) strategy is designed. The fresh seawater is routed into an alkaline/AEM water electrolyzer to sustain stable H2 evolution. The concentrated seawater is fed into a home‐made electrolyzer to produce NaClO and high‐purity Mg(OH)2. A scalable non‐noble metal‐based electrode (50 cm × 50 cm) was designed and fabricated with high activity and stability when applied in the chlorine evolution reaction. System‐level evaluation validates the feasibility of the DDSE strategy. Through rigorous techno‐economic analysis, the unit price of H2 production is reduced to $0.39 kgH2−1 (DOE 2030 target: $1 kgH2−1), and the Global Warming Potential can be reduced up to 6.83%. This proposed DDSE strategy offers a new approach for cost‐effective green hydrogen production with comprehensive seawater valorization.

title: Zwitterionic Thermoplastic Polyurethane‐Based Quasi‐Solid Polymer Electrolytes for Lithium Metal Batteries With Machine‐Learning‐Assisted Mechanistic Insights
content:
A zwitterionic thermoplastic polyurethane electrolyte is synthesized for advanced lithium metal batteries. This unique matrix balances high liquid electrolyte uptake with swelling resistance. It delivers high ionic conductivity, superior toughness, and a high lithium‐ion transference number. Machine‐learning‐assisted molecular simulations reveal a molecular‐level dual‐site mechanism that regulates ions, enabling stable cycling and flexible pouch‐cell operations.








ABSTRACT
This study presents a quasi‐solid‐state electrolyte based on zwitterionic thermoplastic polyurethane (QS‐Z‐TPU) for lithium metal batteries. Unlike conventional quasi‐solid polymer electrolytes that mainly serve as passive liquid‐electrolyte reservoirs, QS‐Z‐TPU is designed as an active ion‐regulating matrix via phosphorylcholine‐derived zwitterionic groups in the TPU framework. The resulting electrolyte combines the elasticity and film‐forming capability of TPU with dual‐site ion regulation, where phosphate sites coordinate Li+ while quaternary ammonium and urethane N‐H groups immobilize TFSI− anions. This design enhances electrolyte affinity while suppressing destructive swelling due to ionic crosslinking. QS‐Z‐TPU exhibits high ionic conductivity, a wide electrochemical stability window, and an enhanced Li+ transference number. Machine‐learning‐assisted molecular modeling further reveals that the zwitterionic oligomer stabilizes separated LiTFSI configurations through cooperative Li+ coordination and TFSI− association, substantially reducing the energetic penalty for ion‐pair separation. This regulated ion environment promotes uniform Li+ flux at the lithium metal interface and facilitates the formation of a stable inorganic‐rich solid electrolyte interphase. Consequently, QS‐Z‐TPU enables stable Li plating/stripping and improves the cycling stability and rate capability of LFP|Li full cells, further validated in flexible pouch‐cell demonstrations. These findings highlight zwitterionic molecular engineering as an effective strategy for interface‐stabilizing quasi‐solid electrolytes.

title: Versatile Acetyl‐Functionalized Phenothiazine Self‐Assembled Monolayers for Efficient Perovskite and Organic Solar Cells
content:
Phenothiazine‐based self‐assembled monolayers with diacetyl functionality serve as universal HTLs for both perovskite and organic solar cells. This strategy enhances device performance while maintaining broad material compatibility and operational stability by improving energy alignment and defect passivation. The polar acetyl groups further induce interfacial dipoles that strengthen the built‐in electric field, enabling efficient hole extraction.








ABSTRACT
The development of versatile, stable, and cost‐effective hole‐transport layers (HTLs) is essential for advancing next‐generation photovoltaic technologies. Herein, we report a series of phenothiazine‐based self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) as HTLs for perovskite and organic solar cells. By systematically tuning the substituents, including unsubstituted phenothiazine (PTZ), dibromo‐PTZ (PTZ‐diBr), and diacetyl‐PTZ (PTZ‐diACE), we achieve control over interfacial energetics and surface properties. The dual coordination sites of carbonyl groups and sulfur in PTZ‐diACE provide Lewis basic sites that coordinate undercoordinated Pb2+ ions, facilitating passivation at the buried HTL/perovskite interface. Additionally, polar acetyl groups induce interfacial dipoles that reinforce the built‐in electric field, promoting efficient hole extraction. Among the series, PTZ‐diACE exhibits superior film formation, a deeper HOMO level, and stronger interfacial interactions, resulting in enhanced charge extraction and suppressed nonradiative recombination. Consequently, inverted perovskite solar cells employing PTZ‐diACE achieve a power‐conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.5% with excellent operational stability, retaining 93% of its initial efficiency after 500 h under the ISOS‐D‐2I protocol. These advantages extend to organic solar cells, where PTZ‐diACE delivers a PCE of 20.4% in D18:L8BO devices and demonstrates compatibility across multiple active layers. This study demonstrates phenothiazine‐based SAMs as HTLs and provides design guidelines for efficient, stable interfacial materials.

title: Asymmetric Cooperative Solvation Structure Enables Entropy‐Enthalpy Compensation for Ultralow Temperature Sodium‐Metal and Sodium–Ion Pouch Cells
content:
The rapid deployment of renewable energy calls for low‐cost, high‐safety, low‐temperature‐tolerant energy storage systems. Sodium‐metal batteries are promising yet plagued by anode corrosion, unstable interfaces, and sluggish ion transport at subzero temperatures. Herein, an electrolyte solvation‐regulation strategy achieves entropy‐enthalpy compensation to rebuild solvation frameworks and optimize SEI, enabling stable Na‐metal cycling in extreme cold and guiding low‐temperature electrolyte design.








ABSTRACT
Sodium‐metal batteries are promising for low‐temperature energy storage, yet conventional electrolytes suffer from an intrinsic trade‐off between thermodynamic stability and kinetic transport, causing salt precipitation and solvation collapse. Herein, an asymmetric cooperative solvation structure (ACSS) is introduced to spatially decouple these conflicting requirements via coordination competition between a strong solvating solvent (diethylene glycol dimethyl ether, DME) and a weak solvating (diethylene glycol diethyl ether, DEE). The DME‐rich inner core forms compact ternary coordination clusters with Na+ and anions (PF6−/BF4−), ensuring enthalpic stability and high salt solubility via geometric ion confinement, while the DEE‐rich outer shell sustains entropic mobility through rapid ligand exchange, facilitating hopping transport and lowering desolvation barriers. This enthalpy–entropy compensation preserves ionic conductivity and structural integrity below −40°C. High anion occupancy within the stable clusters promotes preferential anion reduction, yielding an inorganic‐rich SEI with high mechanical modulus and low Na+ migration energy, effectively suppressing dendrite growth and interfacial polarization. Consequently, Na||Na4Fe3(PO4)2P2O7 pouch cell achieves a capacity retention of 94% at −40°C. Scaled‐up 1.2 Ah hard carbon||Na4Fe3(PO4)2P2O7 and 1.2 Ah hard carbon||NaNi1/3Fe1/3Mn1/3O2 pouch cells sustain 400 and 550 cycles at −30°C and −20°C, respectively, demonstrating the promising practical applicability of this electrolyte design.

title: Light‐Induced Ce–Ov–Ni Motifs Enable Hydrogen‐Poisoning‐Resistant Photothermal NH3 Decomposition
content:
Light irradiation dynamically generates oxygen vacancies at Ni/CeO2 interfaces, forming Ce–Ov–Ni motifs that promote NH3 adsorption and N–H activation while directing hydrogen intermediates to Ni sites. Vacancy‐induced electronic modulation weakens H2 adsorption, accelerates hydrogen release, mitigates hydrogen poisoning, and enables efficient low‐temperature photothermal NH3‐to‐H2 conversion.








ABSTRACT
NH3 is an attractive hydrogen carrier, but efficient H2 release is hindered by N–H bond cleavage and hydrogen poisoning. Herein, we develop Ni nanoparticle‐supported CeO2 (Ni/CeO2) for low‐temperature photothermal NH3 decomposition. Light irradiation is accompanied by the dynamic generation of oxygen vacancies on CeO2, which couple with adjacent Ni sites to form Ce–Ov–Ni motifs, indicating that illumination can regulate the catalyst surface state beyond its thermal contribution. Experiments and DFT calculations indicate that these interfaces create differentiated local environments for NH3 activation and product evolution. Oxygen‐vacancy‐associated sites favor NH3 adsorption, N–H bond activation, and N‐containing intermediates, whereas adjacent Ni sites accommodate H migration and recombination. Moreover, vacancy‐induced electronic modulation weakens H2 adsorption on Ni, thereby facilitating H2 release. Such site differentiation and facilitated hydrogen removal reduce the competitive occupation of active sites by N‐ and H‐containing species and contribute to the resistance to hydrogen poisoning. Under photothermal conditions, 10 wt.% Ni/CeO2 achieves 96.3% NH3 conversion at 450°C, versus 42.5% under thermal catalysis, and maintains >95% conversion at a GHSV of 18,000 mL·gcat−1·h−1. It delivers 20.09 mmol·gcat−1·min−1 H2 with 50 h stability. This work demonstrates light‐induced oxygen‐vacancy–metal interfaces for efficient, hydrogen‐poisoning‐resistant NH3‐to‐H2 conversion.

title: Chemical Coordination and Pore Confinement Enabling a Bifunctional Interface for Accelerated Desolvation and Oriented Deposition Toward Stable Zinc Metal Anodes
content:
A bifunctional interface combining chemical chelation and pore confinement accelerates Zn2+ desolvation and guides oriented Zn(002) deposition, enabling highly stable zinc metal anodes.








ABSTRACT
Aqueous zinc‐ion batteries show great potential for large‐scale energy storage; however, dendrites formation and corrosion on zinc anodes significantly hinder their practical applications. Uneven Zn deposition leads to dendrite growth, while H2O molecules in solvated Zn2+ ions exacerbate surface corrosion and the hydrogen evolution reaction. Herein, we propose a Schiff‐base‐covalently‐grafted UiO‐66‐NH2 metal‐organic framework to construct a bifunctional interface for stable zinc metal anodes. Specifically, the chemical chelation between Schiff base and Zn2+ accelerates desolvation and suppresses side reactions. Meanwhile, the uniformly distributed Zn2+‐chelated sites and the well‐defined confined pore channels of UiO‐66‐NH2 scaffold guide a homogeneous Zn2+ flux and promote Zn(002)‐oriented deposition. As a result, this bifunctional interface enables Zn plating/stripping with a high Coulombic efficiency of 99.8% over 2000 cycles at 5 mA cm−2/1 mAh cm−2. Furthermore, it achieves a capacity retention of over 90% after 4000 charge–discharge cycles in a Zn||MnO2 full cell. This work is expected to open a new avenue for interfacial chemical regulation toward stabilizing zinc metal anodes.

title: Strengthening TMP‐Derived Phosphate SEI via Sn Scaffold and BF4− Interphase Chemistry for Ultra‐Stable, High‐Rate Zn Metal Anodes
content:
A multifunctional additive Sn(BF4)2/H2O (SFB) in a non‐flammable (TMP‐EtOH) organic electrolyte enables a bi‐layered SEI (Sn‐Zn3(PO4)2‐ZnF2@Zn), boosting Zn reversibility via integrated functions of zincophilic Sn, TMP‐derived SEI, anion‐reinforced SEI, EtOH interface modifier, and controlled water content, all provided in a single electrolyte design, affording excellent electrochemical stability and reversibility of the Zn anode.








ABSTRACT
While dynamic solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) construction and solvation engineering have transformed aqueous zinc‐ion batteries, translating these approaches to Organic electrolytes (OE) remains a challenging endeavor due to fundamentally different interfacial environments, solvation thermodynamics, and anion decomposition pathways. Despite providing superior thermodynamic stabilization to Zn anode, OE exhibits low ionic conductivity, thereby limiting operational current densities. Herein, we report the first demonstration of Sn(BF4)2/H2O (SFB) additive integration in a non‐flammable trimethyl phosphate (TMP)‐ethanol (EtOH) (2:1 v/v) OE to architect a gradient SEI interphase on Zn anodes. The multifunctional integration of SFB facilitates the formation of a Sn‐coated Zn surface, a BF41−‐derived SEI@Zn, and H2O molecules as a proton source, collectively contributing to enhanced capacity. This strategic solvent‐salt‐metal synergy enables bi‐layered interfacial engineering within a single electrolyte system, significantly improving the reversibility and stability of the Zn anode. Consequently, SFB enables a robust SEI, achieving exceptional Zn anode durability (7000 h), high‐rate capability (10 mA cm−2), and a high Coulombic efficiency (CE) of 99.8%. Full cells with SFB outperform controls in coin and pouch configurations. Given the rarity of additive(s) in OEs, this study offers a new path to boost stability and lifespan of non‐aqueous Zn batteries.

title: Lignin‐Based Supramolecular Dynamic Networks: A General Platform for Energy Harvesting and Sensing
content:
A rigid–flexible supramolecular design transforms lignin from a passive rigid filler into an active dynamic building block. The resulting ionogel synergistically integrates high stretchability, underwater adhesion, self‐healing, strain sensing, and mechanical energy harvesting, overcoming the persistent trade‐off between robustness and multifunctionality for sustainable flexible electronics.








ABSTRACT
Lignin‐ based ionogels are promising sustainable materials for flexible electronics, yet their development is limited by a persistent tradeoff between mechanical robustness and dynamic multifunctionality. Here, we report a rigid flexible supramolecular design strategy that transforms lignin from a rigid bio‐based component into an active network building block for dynamic ionogels. By coupling rigid lignin derived domains with flexible dynamic polymer segments, the resulting ionogel achieves efficient energy dissipation, reversible network reconstruction, and stable ionic transport. The ionogel exhibits an elongation at break of 1564%, underwater adhesion strength of 488.3 kPa on steel, and near complete self‐healing at room temperature. It further functions as a strain sensor with a gauge factor of 2.83 and stable signal output over 350 stretching cycles. When assembled into a triboelectric nanogenerator, the ionogel delivers a stable voltage output of 75 V under deformation. This work establishes a lignin derived dynamic ionogel platform that integrates robustness, adaptability, sensing, and mechanical energy harvesting for sustainable flexible electronics.

title: Selective Hydrogen Transport Through Polymeric Fullerene Nanosheet Membranes
content:
Polymeric fullerene nanosheets assemble into lamellar membranes containing dense, hourglass‐shaped subnanometer apertures. Transport through these apertures and the interlayer galleries enables rapid, selective H2 permeation, with molecular size and adsorption jointly regulating access and mobility.








ABSTRACT
Lamellar membranes, assembled from two‐dimensional (2D) nanosheets, have attracted intensive attention for molecular and ion sieving due to their tunable interlayer channels and ultrathin selective layers. However, molecular transport in conventional lamellar membranes usually occurs through interlayer galleries whose dimensions vary with stacking, limiting ångström‐scale control over selectivity. Therefore, developing a novel lamellar membrane with ångström‐scale in‐plane pores is highly desirable. In an idealized qTP lattice, four‐directionally connected fullerene cages define periodically distributed apertures that converge from an approximately 5.87 Å entrance to a 3.11 Å waist. Upon assembly, the constriction regions can discriminate by size, while their converging entrances and the intersheet galleries govern molecular access and transport resistance through the in‐plane apertures. The resulting polymeric fullerene nanosheet membrane exhibits an H2 permeance of 3896 ± 107 GPU and an H2/CO2 separation factor of 88.5 ± 5.9 for the separation of an equimolar H2/CO2 mixture at 303.15 K and a total feed pressure of 100 kPa. The separation performance remains stable over 200 h of operation. This study establishes topology‐encoded pore geometry as a design principle for integrating short selective pathways with ångström‐scale molecular discrimination in lamellar membranes.

title: Dichlorobenzodithiophene‐4‐8‐dione Derived Polymer Donor Enables Efficient Thin‐Film/Thick‐Film Organic Solar Cells
content:
A novel electron‐withdrawing block of dichlorobenzodithiophene‐4‐8‐dione is developed to design cost‐effective polymer donor with suppressed non‐radiative energy loss and superior film‐forming kinetics. Its thin‐film (100 nm) device achieved an impressive efficiency (21.1%, certified as 20.6%, ranking among the highest values), while its thick‐film (500 nm) device also obtained a top‐high efficiency (17.3%) among these reported thick‐films (≥500 nm).








ABSTRACT
Polymer donors with electron‐withdrawing benzodithiophene‐4‐8‐dione (BDD) unit play an important role in improving power‐conversion‐efficiency (PCE) of organic solar cells (OSCs), although these achievements rely on high‐cost electron‐donating fluorinated thienyl‐benzodithiophene (BDTT) moiety. Herein, a dichlorobenzodithiophene‐4‐8‐dione (BDD2Cl) unit is developed to design fluorine‐free BDTT‐alt‐BDD2Cl‐structured cost‐effective polymer donor (PBDTT‐BDD2Cl). Compared to its halogen‐free BDTT‐alt‐BDD‐structured control (PBDB‐T), PBDTT‐BDD2Cl shows deep‐shifted energy levels, improved solubility, crystallinity, and packing, tending to suppress energy loss, manipulate film‐forming kinetics, and improve charge transport properties. Accordingly, the PBDTT‐BDD2Cl:L8‐BO device demonstrates dramatically higher photovoltage (0.947 V) and lower non‐radiative energy loss (0.182 eV) and compared to the PBDB‐T:L8‐BO device (0.735 and 0.369 eV), while it achieves decreased PCE. When incorporating it into D18:L8‐BO host, ternary D18:PBDTT‐BDD2Cl:L8‐BO shows optimized donor/acceptor miscibility, delayed material nucleation, and prolonged molecular ordered packing duration, leading to boosted charge dynamics and favorable morphology. Thereby, thin‐film (100 nm) OSC achieves a superior PCE (21.1%, certified as 20.6%, ranking among the highest values) than the D18:PBDB‐T:L8‐BO control (19.3%), while its thick‐film (500 nm) device also obtains a top‐high PCE (17.3%) among these reported thick‐films (≥500 nm). This work highlights that BDD2Cl is an ideal candidate for developing cost‐effective polymer donors toward efficient thin‐film/thick‐film OSCs.

title: Homojunction Back Contacts Enable Efficient Cu2O Photocathodes
content:
A p+/p‐Cu2O back homojunction promotes selective extraction of photogenerated holes and suppresses electron backflow, thereby enhancing the fill factor of Cu2O photocathodes. Coupled with a perovskite solar cell, this integrated architecture drives unassisted tandem overall water splitting with a 7.31% solar‐to‐hydrogen (STH) efficiency, offering a promising route to efficient metal oxide photoelectrodes.








ABSTRACT
Enhancing carrier separation and extraction is crucial to achieve efficient metal oxide photoelectrodes for photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting. Here, we report a highly efficient Cu2O photocathode based on p+/p back‐contact homojunction. The homojunction significantly enhances hole‐selective extraction while suppressing electron backflow at the back‐contact interface, leading to marked improvements in PEC performance. The optimized photocathode delivers a hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) onset potential of 1.1 V and a saturated photocurrent density of ∼8.0 mA cm−2. Furthermore, the p+/p back homojunction design enables the fabrication of a semi‐transparent Cu2O photocathode, which, when integrated with a perovskite solar cell in a tandem configuration, achieves a solar‐to‐hydrogen (STH) efficiency of 7.31%. This work demonstrates a viable strategy for advancing metal oxide photoelectrodes via homojunction engineering.

title: High‐Mobility p‐Type TexSe1‐x Films With Yb‐Enabled Oxidation Suppression for Short‐Wave Infrared Imaging Detection
content:
Yb doping constructs a sacrificial YbOx surface layer to suppress oxidation of p‐type TexSe1‐x films. Optimized 0.2% Yb doping delivers ultrahigh hole mobility. Heterojunction photodetectors realize outstanding short‐wave infrared multispectral imaging with stable optoelectronic performance.








ABSTRACT
Scalable high‐mobility p‐type semiconductor films hold considerable promise for advancing the performance of both photoelectronic devices and complementary metal‐oxide‐semiconductor technologies. Currently, tellurium (Te)‐based semiconductors exhibit high intrinsic hole mobility and compatibility with low‐temperature processing, making them promising candidates for cost‐effective p‐type materials. However, owing to their low Gibbs free energy, they are prone to oxidation into TeO2, which introduces deep‐level defects and severely degrades hole transport, thereby hindering practical applications. Here, we present an effective antioxidant strategy based on ytterbium (Yb) doping, wherein the strong Te–Yb bonding and high oxygen affinity of Yb effectively suppress the oxidation of Te to TeO2, fundamentally stabilizing TexSe1‐x alloys. The resulting Te0.7Se0.3:Yb films exhibit a remarkable hole mobility of 177.5 cm2 V−1 s−1. Furthermore, ZnO/Te0.7Se0.3:Yb photodetectors achieve a high responsivity of 0.21 A/W at 1300 nm, enabling multispectral imaging for precise target discrimination. These results demonstrate the Yb‐enabled oxidation suppression for Te‐based semiconductor, making a crucial stride toward the establishment of commercially viable high‐mobility p‐type semiconductor technology and short‐wavelength infrared photoelectronics.

title: Cross‐System Recycling of Spent Layered Oxides Boosts Synergistic Optimization of Na4Fe3(PO4)2P2O7 Cathodes via Site‐Selective Ni/Mn Co‐Doping
content:
This work proposes a “cross‐system recycling” strategy to transform waste NaNi1/3Fe1/3Mn1/3O2 (NFM) cathode into a Na4Fe2.9Ni0.05Mn0.05(PO4)2P2O7 (NFNMPP) cathode. Benefiting from the synergistic suppressing of impurities and [P2O7] distortion via site‐selective Ni/Mn co‐doping, the NFNMPP material and NFNMPP//HC pouch cells exhibit excellent rate capability, superior cycling stability, a wide operating temperature range, and record‐long cycling life.








ABSTRACT
To address the economic inviability of recycling spent sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs) and the intrinsic drawbacks of Na4Fe3(PO4)2P2O7 (NFPP) cathodes, a “cross‐system recycling” strategy is proposed to transform the waste layered oxides cathodes (NaNi1/3Fe1/3Mn1/3O2, NFM) into high‐performance polyanionic cathodes (Na4Fe2.9Ni0.05Mn0.05(PO4)2P2O7, NFNMPP). Nickel and manganese in the waste NFM that degrades due to “sodium deficiency” and irreversible phase transitions are leached out and doped into the NFNMPP lattice. Benefiting from the synergistic optimization of NFNMPP via site‐selective Ni/Mn co‐doping, the impurities and [P2O7] distortion are suppressed, while the conductivity and Na+ diffusion kinetics are enhanced. Consequently, the high‐purity NFNMPP (91.2%) exhibits an ideal initial coulombic efficiency of 92.84%, remarkable rate capability (75.21 mAh g−1 at 50 C), and excellent cycling stability (86.74% capacity retention after 12 000 cycles at 20 C). Furthermore, paired with hard carbon (HC) anode, NFNMPP//HC pouch cells exhibit high safety, a record‐long cycling life of 5557 cycles, 82.37% capacity retention at 30 C, and a wide operating temperature range (−40°C to 55°C), demonstrating great potential for energy storage applications and powering low‐speed electric vehicles. This study presents a viable pathway for optimizing cathode materials by recycling spent SIBs, and facilitates its practical applications validated by Ah‐level pouch cells.

title: Quasi‐Continuous Multimodal Sensing of Urinary Oxalate Dynamics for Home‐Based Metabolic Monitoring
content:
A multimodal lab‐in‐bucket platform enables continuous, real‐time tracking of urinary oxalate dynamics. By integrating electrochemical oxalate sensing with simultaneous pH and urine volume measurements, this platform corrects matrix drifts that compromise single‐mode analysis. Wireless data transmission facilitates remote home‐based monitoring, while dietary loading experiments reveal distinct oxalate excretion profiles under different dietary patterns. By combining concentration and void volume data, the system establishes a direct correlation between dietary intake and total oxalate load, offering a home‐compatible alternative to conventional 24 h urine analysis.








ABSTRACT
Continuous at‐home monitoring of urinary oxalate dynamics is vital for the comprehensive management of hyperoxaluria and thus reduces the risk of kidney stone formation. However, home‐based devices for capturing dynamic oxalate profiles remain elusive, as urine is challenging to sample and unstable for subsequent biochemical testing. Here we report a remote multimodal sensing platform for achieving such urine monitoring during daily sequential urination through seamless embedding into a standard urine collection bucket. This platform integrates electrochemical oxalate sensing with simultaneous pH and urine‐volume measurements to correct the matrix drift in oxalate quantification. We achieve quasi‐continuous monitoring of 24 h urinary physicochemical dynamics under diet‐induced transient hyperoxaluria. By decoupling oxalate concentration from multimodal signals per urination, we reveal distinct metabolic response profiles under different dietary oxalate loads, providing new real‐time insights into oxalate metabolism and its associated risk of kidney stones. Our all‐in‐one sampling‐and‐testing platform could revolutionize clinical urine analysis for hyperoxaluria, shifting from a one‐time, multi‐day turnaround assay into a paradigm of quasi‐continuous monitoring with immediate feedback. This work represents a practical route toward personalized management of hyperoxaluria and a decentralized metabolic monitoring strategy for urology.

title: Attribution Fingerprinting by Interpretable Machine Learning Reveals Category‐Specific Additive Design Rules for Zinc Anodes
content:
Molecule‐specific SHAP attribution profiles serve as attribution fingerprints that resolve zinc‐electrolyte additives into three attribution‐based categories. Category I screening identifies 2‐fluoropyridine‐5‐carbaldehyde, whose predicted cycle life of 3218 h is confirmed experimentally within 6.5% (3010 h). Structural controls trace the improvement to the aldehyde group, and Zn//MnO2 full cells retain 96% capacity over 4000 cycles.








ABSTRACT
Electrolyte additives are one of the most direct remedy for interfacial instability in aqueous zinc‐ion batteries, yet their development remains empirical. Existing machine‐learning (ML) screening strategies presume a single global structure‐property relationship shared by all additives. Here, an interpretable ML framework predicts cycle life from molecular descriptors and test conditions, and molecule‐specific SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) profiles serve as attribution fingerprints. Unsupervised clustering resolves the additives into three attribution‐based categories, governed respectively by adsorption energetics, charge‐transfer gap and hydrogen‐bond‐network regulation, indicating that one universal descriptor set may not hold across chemically distinct additives. Representative additives from each category, none present in the training set, agree with experiment to within 11%. Category I screening identifies 2‐fluoropyridine‐5‐carbaldehyde (2FPD), predicted at 3218 h, and Zn//Zn cells deliver 3010 h at 1 mA cm−2 and 1 mAh cm−2, within 6.5% of prediction. Structural controls trace the improvement to the aldehyde: retaining it alone gives 900 h against an 89 h baseline, whereas fluorine alone gives 90 h. 2FPD constructs a graded organic‐inorganic interphase that limits water access to the zinc surface and accelerates Zn2+ desolvation, and Zn//MnO2 full cells retain 96% capacity over 4000 cycles. This workflow offers a route towards interpretability‐guided additive design.

title: Sub‐10 nm Confined Channels in Edge‐Closed MXene Nanoribbons Boost Proton Transport for Efficient Single‐Atom Electrocatalysts
content:
Edge‐closed MXene nanoribbons with sub‐10 nm confined channels are fabricated via stiffness‐mediated collapse of nanoscrolls. The unique geometry enhances polarization electric fields, enriching surface protons and accelerating proton transport. Anchoring single‐atom Pt enables exceptional hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) activity, achieving 23 mV overpotential at 10 mA cm−2 and a 25 mV dec−1 Tafel slope.








ABSTRACT
Nanoribbons from atomic layers such as graphene, carbides, and nitrides (MXenes) have attracted considerable interest owing to their distinct quantum confinement effects and high surface activity. However, the controlled synthesis of MXene nanoribbons remains challenging due to their random fragmentation and poor stability. Here, an efficient stiffness‐mediated strategy is developed to fabricate unique edge‐closed MXene nanoribbons, featuring a large aspect ratio of 10∼40 and confined channels of sub‐10 nm at both edges. The key protocol involves modulating the critical collapse pressure by reducing the bending stiffness of MXene layers, thereby triggering the tube collapse of pre‐formed nanoscrolls into edge‐closed nanoribbons upon solvent evaporation. The resulting nanoribbons exhibit an enhanced polarization electric field, leading to a higher surface proton concentration and enhanced proton transport rate compared to nanoscrolls and nanosheets. As a result, these MXene nanoribbons provide an efficient platform for anchoring single‐atom Pt, achieving a low overpotential of 23 mV at 10 mA cm−2 and a Tafel slope of 25 mV dec−1 in the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), outperforming the most reported electrocatalysts.

title: A Retinal Matrix Stiffening Model Reveals FAK‐Dependent Mechanotransduction in Pericytes Underlies Vascular Destabilization
content:
In this study, we show that retinal matrix stiffness is increased in diabetic mice. Using engineered human vascular models with controlled matrix stiffness, we demonstrate that stiffening activates focal adhesion kinase (FAK) signaling in pericytes, suppresses Notch signaling, and disrupts vascular morphology. Human diabetic retinal single‐cell RNA sequencing further supports the relevance of these mechanotransductive pathways in diabetes.








ABSTRACT
Pericyte loss, an early hallmark of diabetic retinopathy (DR), is linked to hyperglycemia and inflammation, whereas the contribution of mechanical changes in the retina remains unclear. We define design parameters for an iPSC‐derived microphysiological system (MPS) comprising pericyte‐endothelial capillary networks embedded in a dynamically stiffening hydrogel engineered to reproduce matrix stiffening in a controlled, human‐relevant context. Microrheology of Ins2Akita mouse retinas revealed increased storage modulus in perivascular regions at a diabetic timepoint coincident with reduced pericyte coverage and vascular remodeling, establishing a stiffness magnitude used to inform the design of the MPS. In the MPS, progressive matrix stiffening alone, in the absence of hyperglycemic exposure, was sufficient to induce analogous vascular defects and to suppress pericyte expression of NOTCH3, HEY1, JAG1, and N‐cadherin in a focal adhesion kinase (FAK)‐dependent manner. Inhibition of FAK restored pericyte signaling and vascular integrity in stiffened conditions without altering soft controls, identifying a FAK‐dependent mechanotransduction as a druggable target. Single‐cell RNA‐sequencing of human diabetic retinas validated enrichment of focal‐adhesion components and alterations in Notch‐pathway transcripts in pericytes. These findings establish a human MPS showing matrix stiffening as a key regulator of pericyte‐mediated vascular stabilization and nominate it and FAK‐dependent mechanotransduction as targets to prevent DR pathogenesis.

title: Anchored Fluoro‐Shielded Solvation for Lithium Metal Batteries
content:
Anchored fluoro‐shielded solvation reconstructs PVDF‐based polymer electrolytes by coupling polyanionic Li+‐solvate sites with fluorinated shielding segments. This design organizes anion‐rich solvation networks, strengthens selective Li+ transport, and generates LiF‐rich solid electrolyte interphase, enabling high conductivity, wide oxidative tolerance, stable Li metal cycling, and long‐term LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2||Li battery operation under demanding high‐voltage and high‐rate conditions.








ABSTRACT
Polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF)‐based polymer electrolytes are promising candidates for solid‐state lithium metal batteries owing to their favorable overall electrochemical properties. However, conventional PVDF‐based polymer electrolytes suffer from uneven solvation distribution, discontinuous ion‐transport pathways, and unstable electrode/electrolyte interfaces caused by residual solvents and porous PVDF frameworks. Herein, we report an anchored fluoro‐shielded solvation strategy to construct a high‐performance PVDF‐based polymer electrolyte. By integrating polyanionic anchoring sites with fluorinated shielding segments, the optimized electrolyte enables spatially distributed anion‐rich solvation pathways, homogeneous Li+ transport, and robust LiF‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). The polymer electrolyte delivers a high ionic conductivity of 1.26×10−3 S cm−1, a Li+ transference number of 0.69, an oxidative onset potential of 5.27 V, and a critical current density of 6.4 mA cm−2. Spectroscopic and interfacial analyses reveal that the anchored fluoro‐shielded solvation structure promotes LiF‐rich SEI formation and suppresses solvent decomposition. Consequently, Li||LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 batteries retain 80.2% capacity after 2000 cycles under high‐voltage and high‐rate conditions of 4.5 V and 5 C. This work highlights anchored fluoro‐shielded solvation as an effective molecular design principle for advanced polymer electrolytes toward practical high‐voltage and high‐rate solid‐state Li metal batteries.

title: Suprasilica Nanosieves for Selective Capture of Aromatics Over Cyclic Aliphatics in Hydrocarbon Feedstocks
content:
Supramolecular silica nanosieves embed hexasila‐ureido‐trianglamine apertures inside a robust silica framework. The hybrid sieves capture benzene and toluene while rejecting cyclohexane and methylcyclohexane, and they hold this preference in vapor, in binary liquids, and in neat naphtha and diluted crude oil. Simulations show that the macrocyclic apertures admit flat aromatic rings and block bulky aliphatic ones, enabling scalable, energy‐efficient hydrocarbon purification.








ABSTRACT
Separating aromatic from cyclic aliphatic hydrocarbons remains a major challenge, as conventional distillation is both energy‐intensive and poorly selective. Here, we report supramolecular silica nanosieves (suprasilica) that integrate organic molecular recognition sites directly into robust inorganic matrices. A hexasila‐ureido‐trianglamine (Δ‐Si6) is co‐condensed within the silica matrix through a self‐assembly sol–gel approach at controlled loadings to produce suprasilica sieves (Δ‐SiNx). In vapor sorption, Δ‐SiNx reject cyclic aliphatic hydrocarbons while displaying high aromatic uptake, achieving benchmark ideal selectivity for benzene over cyclohexane (23.5, uptake 9.4 mmol g−1) on Δ‐SiN20 and for toluene over methylcyclohexane (6.3, uptake 6.3 mmol g−1) on Δ‐SiN10. The selectivity was further confirmed by Dynamic Column Breakthrough experiments, which demonstrated efficient separation under dynamic conditions. Importantly, the Δ‐SiNx retain their molecular discrimination in the binary liquid phase, showing strong preferential uptake while preserving aromatic selectivity in neat naphtha and in diluted crude oil. Metadynamics simulations indicate that the selectivity is kinetic in origin, benzene passing the macrocyclic apertures with a modest barrier while cyclohexane is excluded. These suprasilica nanosieves deliver benchmark separation performance and provide a scalable, energy‐efficient strategy for hydrocarbon purification.

title: Play‐Doh Inspired a Transformative, Shape‐Adaptive iHEÄLS Enabling Post‐Crosslinking Mechanical‐Biological Modulation and Its Effectiveness in Musculoskeletal Repair (Adv. Mater. 61/2026)
content:
Multifunctional Therapeutic Dough
Inspired by Play‐Doh, iHEÄLS transforms the familiar concept of a moldable dough into a multifunctional therapeutic dough. The cover highlights its post‐crosslink programmability, including remarkable extensibility and hemostatic capability; its capacity for mechanical training to reinforce mechanical properties; and its ability to incorporate additional bioactive components. These unique features enable a versatile platform for repairing diverse and irregular tissue defects. More details can be found in the Research Article by Sang Jin Lee, Su Ryon Shin, and co‐workers (DOI: 10.1002/adma.74385).

Fully Soft Electromagnetic Linear Actuator
The image illustrates TESCLA, a tubular electromagnetic soft conformal linear actuator. Liquid‐metal (eGaIn) solenoids wound from silicone microtubes form a bendable soft stator, while compliant magnetic composites serve as the soft mover. Under multi‐step commutation, the actuator generates bidirectional thrust over a large stroke with continuous bending, and senses mover position through solenoid inductance changes. title: Advanced Materials for Biologics Delivery to Brain Tumors
content:
Material innovation is central to unlocking the therapeutic potential of biologics against many central nervous system diseases, including brain cancer. By engineering carriers with controlled transport, targeting, and release properties, advanced materials can overcome the blood–brain barrier and tumor microenvironment, improving the delivery of antibodies, nucleic acids, peptides, and cell‐based therapies for precision neuro‐oncology.








ABSTRACT
Brain cancer remains a major global health challenge due to its high morbidity and mortality. Current standard therapies are often limited by incomplete tumor resection, systemic toxicity, and the inability to effectively penetrate the blood‐brain barrier (BBB), which restricts drug delivery to the tumor site. These challenges underscore the urgent need for innovative therapeutic strategies that can overcome these barriers and improve treatment outcomes. Biological materials encompass a diverse range of molecules, from small peptides to monoclonal antibodies, either derived from living organisms or synthetically synthesized. Unlike traditional therapies, biologics provide a more targeted approach, including specific tumor targeting, immune system modulation, and regenerating damaged cells. Although biologics offer significant promise for brain cancer treatment, major challenges associated with blood–brain and tumour barriers continue to limit their translation, and comprehensive reviews bridging therapeutic advances with delivery technologies remain scarce. While individual biologic classes have been extensively studied, a unified assessment of these modalities and their delivery optimization is still needed. This review addresses the current gap by critically examining recent advances in biologic therapies and evaluating emerging invasive and non‐invasive delivery strategies to enhance their therapeutic efficacy in brain cancer.

title: “Smelltronics”—From Gas to Smell Sensing
content:
The emerging field of smelltronics, encompassing sensing technologies for complex volatile organic compounds, holds significant potential for extracting valuable chemical information. It facilitates the noninvasive, real‐time monitoring of humans, food, and the environment. This review examines the sensing materials, devices, and systems employed for odor detection, addressing current challenges and future perspectives.








ABSTRACT
This review discusses recent trends in smell and odor‐sensing studies, including materials, devices, and interfaces. Since the invention of chemical sensors, particularly over the past few decades, gas sensor materials and devices for small molecules have been extensively investigated. Recently, the social value of odor information has been strongly reaffirmed across diverse research fields, triggered by the rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML). Compared with conventional gas sensing, the requirements for sensing materials and devices for extracting odor information are fundamentally different. In the fields of health diagnosis, food inspection, and environmental monitoring, target molecules that express odor information are frequently composed of molecules with relatively large molecular weights. Because the structural isomers of such relatively large molecules essentially exhibit variations in odor information, their discrimination of such structural isomers is an important issue for smell/odor sensing. Various sensors that operate based on different principles, including electrical, gravimetric, and optical sensors, were discussed in terms of their characteristics. In addition, we describe the sensing materials and interfaces for smell/odor sensing–smelltronics. Finally, we discuss the current challenges and perspectives of smelltronics.

title: Singlet Fission as an Exciton‐Management Platform for Next‐Generation Optoelectronic Materials
content:
Centered on singlet fission (SF), the left half of the TOC graphic illustrates design strategies for SF materials, including structural tuning, energy level engineering, molecular packing and crystal engineering, as well as external factor control; The right half highlights the broad application potential of SF, such as in organic photovoltaics, phototransistors, biomedical imaging, and dye‐sensitized solar cells. Molecular structures and device schematics are used to visually convey current research hotspots and future directions, aligning with the review's comprehensive discussion on SF mechanisms, material optimization, and cross‐disciplinary applications.








ABSTRACT
Singlet fission (SF), the spin‐conserving conversion of one photoexcited singlet exciton into two triplet excitons has emerged as a versatile exciton‐management strategy for optoelectronics and quantum technologies. While initially explored to overcome the efficiency limit of single‐junction photovoltaics, SF is now recognized as a broader platform for engineering correlated excited states. Efficient triplet generation and spin‐correlated pairs create opportunities in photovoltaics, photodetection, photocatalysis, photon up‐conversion, quantum light sources, spin–photon interfaces, and bioimaging. This Review summarizes the fundamental mechanisms, energetic requirements, and molecular design principles governing SF, together with the influence of supramolecular organization and external stimuli on its dynamics. Particular emphasis is placed on the multiscale relationships among molecular energetics, excited‐state character, molecular packing, triplet‐pair separation, triplet transport, and interfacial energy or charge transfer, which ultimately determine device performance. We further discuss recent advances in SF‐enabled optoelectronic and quantum applications. Despite rapid progress, major challenges remain in establishing a unified mechanistic framework, understanding SF in polymeric and disordered systems, and expanding the library of stable, high‐performance SF materials. Finally, we highlight future opportunities in machine‐learning‐assisted materials discovery, excited‐state engineering, and the integration of SF into next‐generation functional optoelectronic devices.

title: Unraveling the Synergistic Catalysis Effect in MOF‐Based Photocatalysts
content:
This review summarizes recent advances in synergistic catalysis within MOF‐based materials, focusing on four core modes: metal–ligand, bimetallic sites, ligand‐ligand and MOF‐based composite synergies. The underlying mechanisms of these synergies are elucidated. Meanwhile, their applications in photocatalytic water splitting, CO2 reduction, and organic transformations are overviewed, with an emphasis on clarifying the relationship between synergistic configuration and photocatalytic performance.








ABSTRACT
Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as promising porous crystalline catalysts for solar‐to‐chemical energy conversion, owing to their customizable structures, large specific surface areas, tunable active sites, and regulatable pore microenvironments. Nevertheless, they still suffer from limitations such as narrow light absorption, rapid charge recombination, insufficient active sites, and poor stability. Synergistic catalysis engineering represents a key strategy to overcome these bottlenecks and enhance the photocatalytic performance of MOF‐based photocatalysts. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in synergistic catalytic effects within MOF‐based materials, focusing on four core synergistic modes: metal‐ligand synergy, bimetallic sites synergy, ligand‐ligand synergy, and MOF‐based composite synergy. The underlying mechanisms of these synergies are elucidated from the perspectives of light absorption regulation, photogenerated charge separation and migration, band structure engineering, and active site modulation. Meanwhile, their applications in photocatalytic water splitting, selective CO2 reduction to C1 and C2+ products, and organic transformations are overviewed, with an emphasis on elucidating the structure–activity relationship between synergistic configuration and photocatalytic performance. Finally, the challenges and future research directions are also proposed, aiming to provide guidance for the rational design of high‐efficiency MOF‐based photocatalysts for solar‐to‐chemical conversion.

title: From Growth to Performance: Emerging Frontiers in Diamond Materials for High‐Performance Devices
content:
Adopting a “growth‐to‐performance” perspective, this review evaluates emerging frontiers in diamond research. It highlights critical progress in chemical vapor deposition synthesis, including large‐area single‐crystal and polycrystalline growth, heteroepitaxy, low‐temperature deposition, and advanced doping. These upstream material breakthroughs directly dictate downstream capabilities, positioning diamond to transform next‐generation optoelectronics, electronics, photonics, and thermal management technologies.








ABSTRACT
Diamond's ultra‐wide bandgap, high carrier mobility, extreme thermal conductivity, and chemical robustness make it a promising platform for next‐generation optoelectronic, electronic, photonic, and thermal technologies. This potential is increasingly unlocked by rapid advances in chemical vapor deposition, enabling precise material synthesis and integration. This review adopts a “growth‐to‐performance” perspective to evaluate emerging frontiers in diamond research. We first highlight critical progress in diamond synthesis, including large‐area single crystal and polycrystalline diamond growth, heteroepitaxy, low‐temperature deposition, and advanced doping strategies. We then examine how these upstream material advancements directly dictate downstream performance across three core technological pillars. In optoelectronics and electronics, these material breakthroughs enable diamond photodetectors, high‐voltage p–n diodes, Schottky barrier diodes, and field‐effect transistors based on both p‐ and n‐type diamond channels. In photonics, advances in nanofabrication and heterogeneous integration are expanding diamond's role in nonlinear optics, integrated photonics, and quantum technologies. In thermal management, diamond heat spreaders integrated with wide‐bandgap semiconductors, coupled with advances in thermal metrology and phonon‐transport modeling, enable superior heat dissipation and reliability. By connecting synthesis with emerging applications, this review outlines the critical pathways through which diamond is poised to play a transformative role in high‐performance technologies across electronics, photonics, and thermal management.

title: Toward Pore‐Engineered 3D‐Printed Materials for Sorption Water Harvesting, Interfacial Evaporation, and Radiative Cooling
content:
Water harvesting, radiative cooling, and interfacial solar evaporation are fundamentally governed by coupled heat, mass, and light transport processes. These processes are mediated by pore architecture, including pore size, connectivity, and hierarchical organization. The engineering of multifunctional porous systems for these real‐world applications is possible by linking bioinspired material design and transport mechanisms with additive manufacturing‐enabled structural control.








ABSTRACT
Water scarcity has intensified interest in passive, sorption‐based atmospheric water harvesting (SAWH), interfacial evaporation (IE), and radiative cooling (RC) technologies that operate at the energy–water–air nexus through coupled heat and mass transfer. Although these approaches are frequently associated with hierarchical porous materials, their performance depends more fundamentally on mesoscale architecture, interfacial design, and system‐level integration than on intrinsic nanoscale porosity alone. Additive manufacturing (AM) offers a versatile platform for engineering such architectures, providing precise control over geometry, connectivity, and functional gradients, while also enabling post‐processing routes to introduce additional porosity where required. Unlike existing reviews that primarily focus on material systems or individual applications, this review establishes a unified manufacturing‐ and pore‐architecture‐centric perspective across SAWH, IE, and RC, emphasizing how AM processing governs transfer behavior and multifunctional performance. This review focuses on the role of AM in structuring porous and semi‐porous materials for SAWH, IE, and RC, with particular emphasis on extrusion‐based methods such as direct ink writing that offer broad material compatibility and process flexibility. We assess the most relevant 3D printing technologies for these applications and discuss their incorporation into operational devices. To address the absence of standardized, application‐specific evaluation methods, we introduce a comprehensive characterization framework linking printing resolution, architectural features, and functional performance, including sorption dynamics, thermal robustness, and multifunctional coupling. Finally, we discuss future opportunities for composite design, system‐level integration, and artificial‐intelligence‐assisted optimization to advance scalable water and thermal management solutions.

title: TESCLA: A Fully Soft Electromagnetic Linear Actuator With Continuous Bending Enabled by Liquid‐Metal Solenoids
content:
TESCLA (tubular electromagnetic soft conformal linear actuator) combines liquid‐metal solenoids and compliant magnetic composites to achieve large‐stroke bidirectional actuation with continuous bending. Integrated inductance‐based self‐sensing enables proprioceptive position estimation without external sensors, providing a versatile platform for soft robotics, biomimetic systems, and wearable haptic devices.








ABSTRACT
Linear actuators are widely employed in robots and wearable devices due to their capability of directly generating linear motion. Although soft actuators and flexible linear actuators have been developed to enable effective operation in various configurations, they are still constrained by a limited actuation range and a discrete bending, which restricts their achievable workspace and curvatures. Here, we propose a tubular electromagnetic soft conformal linear actuator (TESCLA) exerting thrust force over a large actuation stroke with continuous bending. The actuator operates under both a straight configuration and a conformal deformation to the surrounding environment, leveraging the softness of liquid‐metal solenoids (soft stator) and compliant magnetic composites (soft mover). The synchronous actuation strategy allows the actuator to produce controllable bidirectional electromagnetic thrust by applying an electric current to the soft stator. In addition, the step position is estimated by measuring inductance variance of the soft solenoids resulting from the displacement of the soft mover. The design of the actuator components is evaluated through numerical simulations to determine an effective configuration, considering performance characteristics such as thrust force, minimum step size, and sensing resolution. By utilizing the functionalities of the proposed actuator, biomimetic robotic applications and a wearable haptic device were demonstrated.

title: Nonequilibrium Interfacial Complexation Fibers With Programmable Ionic Memory
content:
Two aqueous polyelectrolyte droplets initiate nonequilibrium interfacial polyelectrolyte complexation (IPC) under ambient conditions, spontaneously generating multiscale fibers. Assembled into functional networks, these fibers exhibit spatio‐temporal summation analogous to biological synapses, and demonstrate programmable ionic memory spanning several orders of magnitude in timescale, turning a simple pair of droplets into an intelligent platform capable of pixel‐level information encoding.








ABSTRACT
Emulating learning and memory functions of biological systems in soft, textile‐compatible materials remains challenging, particularly for artificial synapses that require both structural adaptability and reliable ionic dynamics. Existing artificial synaptic devices predominantly rely on membrane‐based or multilayered architectures, which complicate fabrication and limit scalability. Here, we report multiscale interfacial polyelectrolyte complexation (IPC) fibers fabricated via a one‐step interfacial process, enabling programmable fiber architectures with mechanical compliance and direct compatibility with smart textile platforms. The IPC fibers exhibit hierarchical structures spanning nanometer to micrometer length scales, promoting confined ionic transport and slow relaxation dynamics within flexible, thread‐like conductors. As a result, fiber‐based artificial synapses display pronounced short‐term plasticity with a tunable slow relaxation time constant (τ2), which spans several orders of magnitude and reaches up to 40 min owing to multiscale ion trapping and migration. Moreover, woven fiber arrays demonstrate both temporal and spatial summation of synaptic responses, enabling time‐dependent learning and pixel‐level memory encoding in IPC fiber arrays. The facile, environmentally benign fabrication strategy, combined with intrinsic structure‐function coupling in IPC fibers, establishes a versatile material and device platform for potential smart textiles, wearable neuromorphic systems, and adaptive fabrics.

title: Inductively Expandable Supraparticles as Microscopic Force Generators for Remote Mechanical Actuation
content:
This study demonstrates the combination of magnetic nanoparticles and functional blowing agents into supraparticles. Upon induction heating, they actuate via rapid gas generation or extensive volume expansion. These supraparticles lift up to 25 000 times their own mass and rapidly open cured epoxy resins, providing a versatile strategy for fast micron‐scale pressure actuation.








ABSTRACT
Generating strong mechanical forces at the microscale is central to emerging technologies like soft microrobotics and adaptive materials. However, delivering energy remotely and converting it into mechanical work within confined environments remains challenging. Magnetic nanoparticles enable rapid, contactless heat generation through induction heating under alternating magnetic fields, yet this is typically exploited only for thermal effects. Here, we introduce micrometer‐scaled supraparticle additives that convert induction‐generated heat directly into mechanical work through confined expansion. These supraparticles are fabricated by spray‐drying magnetic nanoparticles with functional blowing agents, enabling actuation by rapid gas release using azodicarbonamide or volumetric expansion via vaporization‐induced volume expansion within a superabsorbent poly(acrylamide‐co‐acrylic acid) network. Upon magnetic excitation, heating generates pressure within the supraparticles, yielding power densities up to 5 kW kg−1 and lifting capabilities of up to 25 000 times their own mass, exceeding the typical limit of conventional materials (∼10 000x). Actuation is achieved with heating times of ≤5 s and total energy consumption below 3 Wh, remaining reproducible over multiple actuation cycles without failures. Generated stresses are sufficient to disrupt mechanically stable matrices, including rigid epoxies. These results establish supraparticles as versatile platforms for remotely powered mechanical actuation, enabling localized stress generation and material disruption in interactive materials.

title: Spectrally Coordinated Plasmonic–Photothermal Photocatalysts for Mineralization of Mixed Indoor VOCs Under White LED Illumination
content:
A plasmonic–photothermal–photocatalytic hybrid comprising Cu(II)‐grafted TiO2, yolk–shell Au@SiO2, and reduced graphene oxide sheets (CuT/AuSi‐GS) harvests full‐spectrum white light‐emitting diode (LED) light via complementary photocatalytic oxidation, localized surface‐plasmon‐resonance‐induced electric‐field enhancement, and photothermal acceleration. The tri‐functional architecture drives mineralization of aliphatic and aromatic volatile organic compounds under white LED illumination, highlighting its promise as an LED‐driven photocatalyst platform for indoor air purification.








ABSTRACT
Indoor volatile organic compounds (VOCs) remain a major health concern, yet conventional photocatalysts show limited effectiveness under low‐intensity indoor lighting. Here, a spectrally coordinated plasmonic–photothermal–photocatalytic architecture integrating Cu(II)‐grafted TiO2 (CuT), yolk–shell Au@SiO2 (AuSi), and reduced graphene oxide sheets (GS) is presented for efficient mixed‐VOC mineralization under white light‐emitting diode (LED) illumination. Rather than acting as a simple multicomponent composite, this architecture couples partially overlapping but preferential spectral contributions across the LED spectrum: CuT drives visible‐light photocatalytic oxidation, AuSi contributes localized surface‐plasmon‐resonance‐induced electric‐field enhancement near CuT, and GS converts longer‐wavelength photons into localized heat to accelerate interfacial oxidation kinetics. Compared with CuT and binary controls, the composite enhances reactive oxygen species generation, CO2 formation, and humidity tolerance. CuT/AuSi‐GS enables near‐stoichiometric CO2 formation during CH3CHO/C7H8 mixed‐VOC mineralization at 10 ppmv within 1 h and maintains over 80% CO2 yield throughout 168 h of continuous‐flow operation at 2 ppmv. Chamber‐scale validation in a 64‐L reactor indicates the feasibility of VOC mineralization under a dedicated white LED source. Operando infrared spectroscopy traces stepwise oxidation of oxygenated and aromatic VOCs toward CO2, while wavelength‐dependent activity, spectral‐overlap analysis, thermal profiling, complementary spectroscopy, and simulations support coordinated energy utilization and deep mineralization under indoor white LED illumination.

title: Oxygen‐Configuration‐Driven Anionic Redox Regulation for High‐Voltage NaNi1/3Fe1/3Mn1/3O2
content:
Fe migration from the TM layers to the Na layers in high‐voltage NaNi1/3Fe1/3Mn1/3O2 generates ARR‐active oxygen configurations, thereby activating ARR and promoting oxygen loss and structural degradation. Pre‐occupation of Na sites by Ca effectively suppresses Fe migration and ARR activation, mitigates oxygen loss, and preserves the layered framework during high‐voltage cycling.








ABSTRACT
To boost the energy density of sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs), elevating the operating voltage (≥4.2 V) of NaNi1/3Fe1/3Mn1/3O2 (NFM) cathodes is imperative, while inherently triggers irreversible anion redox reactions (ARR). Unfortunately, the activation mechanism of ARR in NFM has yet to be clearly elucidated, and the targeted regulation remains a significant challenge. Herein, the oxygen redox course in NFM is investigated, and the activation of ARR can be attributed to the generation of □‐O‐□ and □‐O‐Na configurations with high‐energy unhybridized O 2p nonbonding orbitals, which origins from the Fe3+ migration from the transition metal layer to the Na layer. To mitigate the formation of ARR‐activated oxygen configurations, a pre‐occupation strategy in the Na layer is proposed to suppress Fe3+ migration, which significantly reduces O–O dimerization and oxygen evolution. Meanwhile, the activity and reversibility of Fe redox is markedly improved by the stabilized layered structure. Benefiting from the robust lattice oxygen, the modified sample exhibits excellent cycling performance with an ultrahigh capacity retention up to 70% after 1500 cycles at 5 C. This work establishes a direct link between oxygen configuration evolution and ARR irreversibility and provides a rational design principle for high‐voltage NFM.
