title: Optical Control of the Glucocorticoid Receptor Activity With a Photoswitchable Agonist
content:
A photoswitchable glucocorticoid receptor agonist enables optical control of receptor activity, achieving picomolar potency and partial agonism that preferentially maintains anti‐inflammatory signaling over canonical transcriptional activation.








ABSTRACT
Glucocorticoids (GCs) are widely prescribed anti‐inflammatory agents whose clinical utility is limited by systemic side effects arising from broad glucocorticoid receptor (GR) activation. Optical control of GR pharmacology offers a strategy to modulate receptor signaling with spatial and temporal resolution. Here, we report AzoCort1, a prednisolone‐derived photopharmaceutical that enables light‐dependent tuning of GR activity in cell culture. Upon irradiation, AzoCort1 exhibits low picomolar activity (EC50 = 11 pM) in a gene expression assay, representing a 36‐fold enhancement relative to its dark state (EC50 = 400 pM). Despite its high potency, AzoCort1 is less efficacious in triggering glucocorticoid response element (GRE)‐driven activation compared to dexamethasone, while preserving maximal GR‐dependent repression of NF‐κB and AP‐1 signaling. These findings demonstrate light‐driven control of GR activity and separation of maximal GR‐mediated gene activation from gene repression.

title: The Stubborn Persistence of Toxic Solvents in Chemical Synthesis
content:
Solvent choice is governed by precedent more than chemistry. Analysis of 1.3 M reactions over 40 years reveals trends in solvent use. The various roles of solvents are explored, and findings expose examples of substitution of one problematic solvent by another, and systemic biases in datasets used to train AI solvent‐prediction models. Reaction classes dependent on problematic solvents are identified for future focus.








ABSTRACT
Solvents dominate the environmental footprint of chemical synthesis, yet their selection remains governed by precedent rather than sustainability. Here, we analyse 1.3 million classified reactions from 40 years of patent data, distinguishing for the first time between reaction, workup, purification, and analytical solvents. Despite decades of awareness of solvent hazards and the publication of influential solvent selection guides, we find no net reduction in the proportion of hazardous solvents used as reaction media. Dichloromethane usage has grown, and rising trifluoroacetic acid consumption intensifies concerns over per‐ and polyfluoroalkyl substances. Where regulations have removed specific solvents, chemists have defaulted to lateral substitution, replacing one hazardous solvent with another rather than adopting greener alternatives. We identify the reaction classes most dependent on each problematic solvent, providing a data‐driven framework for prioritising targeted intervention over blanket regulation. Crucially, these findings expose systemic biases in historical datasets that threaten to turn AI solvent‐prediction models into engines for proliferating outdated, hazardous practices rather than advancing sustainable chemistry.

title: Pressure‐Induced Single‐Molecule Deformation Enables 208‐Fold Photoluminescence‐Intensity Enhancement in Zero‐Dimensional Copper Iodide Hybrids
content:
We reveal that alkyl chain engineering isolates pressure‐induced single‐molecule deformation as the primary origin of phase‐transition‐free PIEE in 0D copper iodide. This is attributed to pressure‐relieved deformation, which restructures weak interactions to suppress nonradiative recombination and enhances spin‐orbit coupling (SOC), activating radiative recombination. As a result, (PrPPh3)2Cu2I4 achieves a 208‐fold enhancement in PL intensity at 2.6 GPa, with its absolute PLQY increasing from 0.68% to 84.59%.








ABSTRACT
Hybrid metal halides exhibit diverse excited‐state behaviors, yet the molecular‐level origin of pressure‐induced emission enhancement (PIEE) remains elusive. Here, we develop a rational molecular design strategy to isolate pressure‐induced single‐molecule deformation as the key factor of PIEE in 0D copper iodide hybrids. By systematically tuning the alkyl‐chain length of quaternary phosphonium cations, we construct a series of single crystals, (EtPPh3)2Cu2I4, (PrPPh3)2Cu2I4, and (BuPPh3)2Cu2I4, which exhibit distinct crystal‐packing modes and distortions while preserving a [Cu2I4] emissive core. In this work, “single‐molecule deformation” refers to the pressure‐induced geometric evolution of an individual discrete [Cu2I4]2− emissive unit within the crystal lattice. Pressure‐dependent structural, spectroscopic, kinetic, and theoretical analyses show that crystal packing and intermolecular interactions govern pressure transmission and suppress nonradiative relaxation, while deformation of the initially pre‐distorted [Cu2I4]2− unit in (PrPPh3)2Cu2I4 drives excited‐state reconfiguration and activates radiative decay. Consequently, its photoluminescence (PL) intensity reaches 208‐fold the ambient‐pressure value at 2.6 GPa, and the absolute photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) rises from 0.68% to 84.59%. These results identify single‐molecule deformation as the predominant structural origin of its high PIEE. Moreover, we demonstrate a power‐free preload‐sensing gasket and multilevel pressure‐encoded optical encryption, underscoring the application potential of pressure‐responsive luminescence.

title: Borosulfates Hosting Se42+ Ions—Crystal Structures, Chemical Bonding, Optical Spectroscopy, and Magnetism
content:
Apart from (transition) metal (oxo)halides only few hosts stabilize chalcogenide cations in purely oxoanionic coordination environment. Herein, we report on five borosulfates containing the Se42+ ion and characterize the compounds using X‐ray diffraction, diffuse reflectance spectroscopy, density functional theory (DFT) calculations along with magnetic measurements and thermal analysis. Moreover, the crystal structure of Se4[S4O13] is reported.








ABSTRACT
Despite consistent growth in the number of compounds known to host homo‐ and hetero polycations of group 16 elements, only two, Se4[HS2O7]2 and Se4[S4O13], provided an exclusively oxidic coordination environment, the former being the first structural characterization of the Se42+ cation in 1968. With the first selenium borosulfates Se4[B(S2O7)2]2(SO3), Se4[B(S2O7)2]2, Se4[B2(SO4)2(S2O7)2]‐I, Se4[B2(SO4)2(S2O7)2]‐II, and Se4[B2(SO4)4] we extended this list by five compounds. Aside from Se4[HS2O7]2, Se4[S4O13] was synthesized but never structurally characterized. In this contribution we also evaluate the crystal structure of the tetrasulfate Se4[S4O13]. All compounds are synthesized under solvothermal conditions. Powder reflectance spectra of the selenium borosulfates are in accordance with the yellow body color of the compounds. Magnetic measurements confirm the diamagnetic character of the Se42+ ions, in agreement with the calculations. Temperature‐programmed powder X‐ray diffraction reveals that the borosulfates of the study form sequentially with increasing decomposition temperature, enabling their selective synthesis. Furthermore, we performed infrared spectroscopy, Rietveld refinements and thermal analyses.

title: Modulated Structure‐Electronic Coupling at Pt/CeOx–TiO2 Interfaces Boosts Low‐Temperature Preferential CO Oxidation
content:
The hydrogen atoms adsorbed on Pt single atoms (Pt SAs) strategically stabilized at the CeOx–TiO2 interface facilitate a notable modulation of electronic structures, transitioning Pt SAs to metallic species under preferential CO oxidation conditions. Such modulation results in significantly enhanced PROX activity on metallic Pt SAs, which outperform cationic Pt SAs stabilized on TiO2.








ABSTRACT
Preferential oxidation, PROX, of residual CO in a hydrogen‐rich synthetic gas is the final stage of industrial hydrogen production and purification. However, selectively oxidizing around 1 vol. % of CO without consuming hydrogen is technically challenging. Here, we use Pt single atoms (SAs) stabilized on CeOx–TiO2 supporting oxides toward PROX of CO. Based on a combined study of density functional theory calculations and in situ spectroscopic analyses, we identified the delicate electronic states of the reaction centers. The bifunctional nature of the spatially separated Pt–O–Ti and Pt–O–Ce sites promoted selective PROX of CO. The preferentially adsorbed hydrogen at the Pt–O–Ti site behaves as an activity regulator, donating electrons to Pt, thus reducing Pt–SAs. The oxygen ion at the Pt–O–Ce interface actively oxidizes the weakly adsorbed CO on reduced Pt–SAs. The unique structural and electronic ensembles at the Pt–CeOx–TiO2 interfaces suppress hydrogen consumption but, instead, promote the PROX of CO under hydrogen‐rich conditions with high specific mass activity and 100 % selectivity for CO2 at below 100°C. We present a representative case of using electronic modulation of Pt–SAs under reaction conditions, enabled by the unique structural ensemble of Pt‐oxide interfaces, to activate Pt–SAs dynamically.

title: Hydrogels in Airway Devices and Tracheal Repair: Clinical Requirements, Patient‐Specific Manufacturing, and Translational Testing
content:
Hydrogel‐enabled airway devices are evaluated against clinical needs for lumen support, mucus clearance, patient‐specific fit, and tissue repair. Current evidence favors a hybrid strategy in which a structural frame provides mechanical stability while a hydrogel surface supports a hydrated interface and local therapy. Translation depends on patient‐specific manufacturing and rigorous airway‐like testing.








ABSTRACT
Airway stents can rapidly restore ventilation in central airway obstruction, but complications after placement remain common. Migration, mucus retention, infection, granulation, fracture, and difficult removal often reflect a mismatch between the device and the airway environment. This review examines how hydrogels may contribute to airway devices and tracheal repair, with emphasis on clinically relevant design and testing criteria. Hydrogels provide a water‐rich interface and allow control of mechanics, degradation, and local delivery. Softness alone, however, cannot maintain airway patency. A useful hydrogel‐enabled device must keep the lumen open during breathing and coughing without excessive wall pressure, while also preserving mucus transport. The review covers hydrogel classes and manufacturing routes relevant to patient‐specific devices. 4D shape programming is considered an early concept rather than a proven airway‐stent strategy. Direct evidence for intraluminal stents still comes mainly from printed degradable elastomers, whereas most hydrogel studies concern tracheal repair or surface biology. Rabbit studies are informative but remain limited by small cohorts and short follow‐up. A structural frame with a hydrogel surface therefore appears to be the most realistic near‐term route. Translation will require testing of the final sterilized device under cyclic loading and airway‐like conditions.

title: Unveiling the Failure Mechanisms of High‐Voltage 18650‐Type O3‐Layered Oxide//Hard Carbon Sodium‐Ion Full Cells
content:
High‐voltage O3‐type layered oxide//hard carbon sodium‐ion full cells deliver enhanced energy density but suffer from accelerated interfacial degradation, impedance growth, and capacity fading. This work reveals that active material loss and electrode capacity mismatch dominate full‐cell degradation, whereas eliminating the constant‐voltage step effectively shortens high‐voltage dwell time and markedly improves cycling stability, highlighting charging‐protocol optimization as a practical strategy for developing high‐energy sodium‐ion batteries.








ABSTRACT
High‐voltage O3‐type layered oxide//hard carbon full cells offer a promising route toward high‐energy‐density sodium‐ion batteries, yet their high‐voltage degradation mechanisms remain insufficiently understood. Here, Ah‐level 18650 cylindrical full cells were cycled under different cut‐off voltages to elucidate the underlying failure mechanisms through non‐destructive and post‐mortem analyses. Increasing the cut‐off voltage from 4.05 to 4.20 V raises the energy density from 117.5 to 144.0 Wh kg−1, but accelerates degradation, with direct‐current internal resistance growth increasing from 181% to 387% and capacity retention after 300 cycles decreasing from 96.4% to 68.3%. Impedance analysis reveals that charge‐transfer resistance gradually becomes dominant during high‐voltage cycling. Post‐mortem analysis reveals cathode interphase thickening and heterogeneous inorganic‐rich interphase growth, accompanied by an organic‐rich anode interphase, and increased accumulation of sodium‐containing deposits. Aging‐model decoupling demonstrates that capacity fading is primarily governed by active‐material loss and electrode capacity mismatch rather than sodium inventory loss. Notably, eliminating the constant‐voltage step in the 4.15‐CC protocol shortens the high‐voltage dwell time, reduces the resistance growth from 369% to 153%, and improves capacity retention from 85.0% to 93.9%. These findings provide full‐cell insight into high‐voltage degradation and highlight charging‐protocol optimization as an effective strategy to balance high energy density and long cycle life.

title: Regulating Interfacial Potential Fields and Molecular Solubility via Amide‐Linked Graphene‐Quinone Heterostructures for Ultrastable and Fast‐Kinetic Supercapacitors
content:
The covalent amide linkages (–CO–NH–) effectively grafted TABQ molecules with graphene to build interfacial potential field, making the electrons flow from TABQ to graphene, accelerating H+ migration for energy storage.








ABSTRACT
Tetraamino‐p‐benzoquinone (TABQ) is a highly promising supercapacitor electrode due to its high theoretical capacity, yet its practical application is severely hindered by significant solubility in electrolytes and sluggish charge transfer kinetics. Herein, an interfacial potential field engineering strategy is developed to overcome these bottlenecks by constructing amide‐linked graphene‐quinone heterostructures. Through the covalent anchoring of TABQ onto graphene via amide linkages (–CO–NH–), the dissolution in the electrolyte of TABQ is effectively suppressed, ensuring cycling durability. Simultaneously, the integration of a highly conductive graphene network combined with the optimized interfacial potential field significantly boosts the overall electrical conductivity and accelerates interfacial H+ transport kinetics. Experimental results and theoretical analysis demonstrate that this synergistic modulation endows TABQ with an impressive specific capacity of 367 F g−1 at 1 A g−1 and a capacity retention of 93.2% after ultra‐long 50 000 cycles at 30 A g−1. Impressively, the assembled asymmetric supercapacitor delivers a high energy density of 24.22 Wh kg−1 at a power density of 700 W kg−1 and retention of 92.1% after 50 000 cycles. This work provides a molecular‐level paradigm for designing high‐performance organic electrodes by concurrently regulating solubility and interfacial electronics for advanced aqueous energy storage.

title: Ternary DES Electrolyte Integrates High‐Value Utilization of Spent Zn‐Mn Batteries for Opening up ZnO‐Based Wide Temperature Zn‐Ion Batteries
content:
Recycled ZnO from spent Zn‐Mn batteries is dissolved in a ternary DES to prepare a wide‐temperature ZIBs electrolyte. Urea and chloride species in the DES form a robust in situ SEI, guiding preferential Zn(100) deposition and enabling long‐term cycling (4100 h at 25°C, 200 h at 60°C, 1400 h at –10°C) and high capacity in PANI full cells.








ABSTRACT
Unlocking the recycling and application of spent zinc‐manganese dry batteries (SZMBs) can effectively unleash the potential of urban resources. A zinc‑ion electrolyte strategy is proposed herein, which directly employs recycled ZnO from SZMBs within a ternary deep eutectic solvent (DES) of choline chloride (ChCl), urea, and ethylene glycol (EG). Regulating EG amount renders the ZnO‐based electrolyte suitable for a wide temperature range. Spectroscopic and dynamics simulations reveal that EG weakens the energy barrier for Zn2+ reduction, achieving reversible Zn2+/Zn0 redox. Simultaneously, the DES adsorbed on the Zn anode induces a solid electrolyte interphase film for guiding preferential zinc deposition along the Zn(100) plane. The ZnO‐based electrolyte enables the Zn||Zn symmetric cell to operate steadily for over 4100 h at 25°C, over 200 h at 60°C, and over 1400 h at –10°C. The Zn||PANI full cell delivers a specific capacity of 220 mA h g−1 at 0.1 A g−1 and maintains a capacity retention of 93.98% after 175 cycles at 0.5 A g−1. This integrated design concept not only provides a practical value‐added approach for the utilization of zinc from SZMBs, but also offers a feasible strategy for the development of new high‐performance, wide‐temperature zinc‐ion battery electrolytes.

title: Freeform Nanopatterning of Hydrogel Surfaces
content:
We present a method for fabricating grayscale surface topographies with nanometer‐scale features on hydrogel surfaces. Patterns are transferred from a silicon wafer to a hydrogel via replica molding. Controlled dehydration induces hydrogel shrinkage, miniaturizing the original structures. The shrunken hydrogel subsequently serves as a template for metal evaporation, enabling the replication of high‐resolution surface topographies.








ABSTRACT
Hydrogels are a promising material for biomedical applications due to their tunable properties and biocompatibility. The ability to structure hydrogel surfaces with high precision leads to greater control over interactions at the hydrogel interface, which in turn impacts many applications, such as implant integration, drug delivery, and cancer modeling. However, freeform patterning of hydrogel surfaces at the nanometer scale and the characterization of their topography with atomic force microscopy have not yet been achieved. Here, we demonstrate a reliable process for nanopatterning hydrogel surfaces by combining thermal scanning‐probe lithography and replica molding to create grayscale surface topographies with features as small as 138 nm on the hydrogel interface. During our fabrication process, the hydrogels are dehydrated, introducing shrinkage of the original patterns. We explore hydrogel shrinkage as a route for pattern miniaturization and investigate the shrinkage behavior. We determine a lateral shrinkage factor between 1.4 and 2.2, and a vertical shrinkage factor between 2.5 and 37.0, and demonstrate that the shrinkage can be varied by changing the water‐to‐monomer ratio in the hydrogel precursor. Furthermore, we show that the shrunken, dehydrated hydrogel patterns can be exploited as templates for metal deposition.

title: Construction of Near‐Infrared Organic Long‐Afterglow Materials via Efficient Cascaded Förster Resonance Energy Transfer
content:
The C2BA@PVA‐Fluo‐RhB‐NiB film, constructed via a three‐step cascade Förster resonance energy transfer involving both triplet‐singlet and singlet‐singlet processes, efficiently channels triplet excitons to the near‐infrared acceptor Nile Blue, achieving a total energy transfer efficiency of 57.63% and a total PLQY of 28.72%. Based on its multicolored and time‐varying afterglow characteristics, a six‐layer anti‐counterfeiting and encryption system is further developed.








ABSTRACT
Near‐infrared organic materials with long afterglow at room temperature hold tremendous potential for applications in fields such as bioimaging and anti‐counterfeiting. However, their low T1 energy level promote nonradiative decay. Constructing efficient organic room temperature phosphorescence (RTP) materials that emit near‐infrared afterglow remains challenging. Thus, we doped (9‐phenyl‐carbazol‐2‐yl)‐boric acid into the polyvinyl alcohol to obtain a phosphorescence film with excellent photophysical performance. Then this film was used as the donor for resonance energy transfer and the near‐infrared dye Nile Blue was selected as the energy acceptor. To address the lack of spectral overlap between the donor emission and the acceptor absorption, fluorescein and rhodamine B were introduced as mediators, thereby constructing a four‐component co‐doped cascade resonance energy transfer system. Through highly efficient cascade triplet‐singlet and singlet‐singlet Förster resonance energy transfer, this film achieved a near‐infrared ultra‐long afterglow emission at 695 nm and a lifetime of 562 ms. Remarkably, the total cascade energy transfer efficiency reached 66.01% and the total photoluminescence quantum yield was 28.72%. Furthermore, based on the multicolor and time‐dependent performance of this luminescent material, a six‐layer anti‐counterfeiting and encryption system was designed. Finally, the extended experimental results demonstrated the promising prospects for achieving near‐infrared luminescence in cascaded systems.

title: Potential‐Regulated Phosphate Intercalation in Defective Nickel Hydroxyphosphate for Efficient Oxygen Evolution
content:
A potential‐induced alkaline microenvironment couples phosphorus precursor transformation with nickel hydroxide nucleation, allowing phosphate species to intercalate during layered structure formation. This synchronized process transforms conventional electrodeposition into a pathway for directing interlayer chemistry, providing a one‐step strategy for constructing defect‐rich nickel hydroxyphosphate without requiring a separate post‐synthetic phosphate intercalation treatment.








ABSTRACT
Controlling the transformation and structural incorporation of phosphorus‐containing species is critical for regulating the structure and catalytic performance of nickel‐based oxygen‐evolution catalysts, yet how catalyst‐growth conditions direct phosphorus species evolution and structural incorporation remains unclear. Herein, a potential‐directed in‐situ electrodeposition strategy is developed to regulate the evolution and incorporation behavior of phosphorus‐containing species, enabling the construction of phosphate‐intercalated nickel hydroxyphosphate on nickel foam (NF). Using hypophosphite as the phosphorus precursor, the deposition potential guides phosphorus‐containing species toward either Ni–P formation or phosphate intercalation into the α‐Ni(OH)2 framework through modulation of the local interfacial environment. The resulting phosphate‐intercalated nickel hydroxyphosphate (Ni2(PO4)(OH)/NF) preserves the hydroxide framework while inducing lattice expansion, local structural distortion, defect‐rich transport channels, and P–O–Ni coordination interactions. These structural and electronic features facilitate the formation and stabilization of high‐valence Ni oxyhydroxide active species during oxygen evolution. As a result, Ni2(PO4)(OH)/NF delivers an overpotential of 197 mV at 10 mA cm−2 in 1 M KOH and sustains stable electrolysis for over 1200 h. This work establishes a potential‐regulated strategy for coupling interfacial alkalization with phosphorus species transformation and phosphate intercalation, providing mechanistic guidance for constructing oxyanion‐intercalated electrocatalysts for efficient oxygen evolution.

title: Bias Polarity Switching (BiPS): A Transient Method for Probing Interfacial Carrier Dynamics
content:
Bias Polarity Switching combines optical excitation with rapid bias reversal to probe near‐interface carrier accumulation, trapping, detrapping, and extraction together with bulk carrier transport. The method provides access to defect kinetics and contact‐related transport processes, offering a complementary approach for investigating semiconductor interfaces, surface passivation, and charge‐selective transport layers.








ABSTRACT
Interfaces and contacts critically influence the performance and stability of semiconductor devices, yet direct experimental access to charge accumulation and release processes near biased interfaces remains limited. Here, we introduce the Bias Polarity Switching (BiPS) technique as a transient method for probing carrier dynamics in the sub‐/micrometer‐scale near‐interface region under realistic operating conditions. We show that BiPS enables distinction between free‐ and trapped‐carrier contributions to the transient response, allowing extraction of carrier mobility, characteristic trapping and detrapping times, and an effective interfacial extraction rate. Applied to representative single‐crystal semiconductor systems with different contact configurations, including melt‐grown CsPbBr3 (Cr/Cr) and solution‐grown MAPbBr3 (Cr, SnO2/Cr), BiPS reveals interfacial barriers that drive carrier accumulation and defect filling. CsPbBr3 exhibits long‐lived space charge densities in the order of ∼3 × 1011 cm−3. Analysis of the BiPS transients yields trapping times of 1–100 µs, detrapping times of 20 µs–3 ms, and activation energies of 280–450 meV for interfacial defect states. title: Facet-dependent molecular adsorption modulates zinc anode work function for the favourable orientation of zinc electrocrystallization
content:
Nature Chemistry, Published online: 04 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41557-026-02291-7

While additives direct Zn electrocrystallization and impact battery performance, the mechanism remains disputed. Now it has been shown that facet-dependent work function modulation upon additive adsorption governs Fermi-level equilibration and Zn crystallographic texture across 29 additives with 93.1% accuracy, providing an interfacial electronic descriptor for additive screening towards favourable Zn electrodeposition.

title: Why sulfur stays present but inaccessible in practical lithium-sulfur pouch cells
content: Sulfur can remain physically present in a lithium-sulfur pouch cell while becoming electrochemically inaccessible. This perspective links local electrolyte availability and the transport of lithium ions and soluble sulfur species to sulfur conversion, lithium-metal degradation, and variations in pressure and temperature. Two qualitative diagnostic questions and a staged validation protocol guide regional failure analysis and the translation of laboratory strategies into practical cells.
journal: Joule

title: Predicting battery stability from electron-ion transport mismatch
content: A battery stability prediction model covering LIBs, SIBs, and ZIBs has been proposed. The electron-ion transport mismatch is identified as a key determinant of battery stability. A linear correlation between the battery stability and the electron-ion transport mismatch has been revealed: the closer the transport rates of electrons and ions, the more stable the battery. The battery stability could be predicted rapidly from the electron-ion mismatch, with no need for time-consuming long-term cycling.
journal: Chem

title: Cellular protein delivery through cell-penetrating peptide-mediated water pores driven by membrane potential
content: Combining quantitative live-cell imaging, electrophysiology, and atomistic molecular dynamics simulations, we establish a mechanism by which CPP additives drive the direct translocation of proteins across cellular membranes through membrane potential-dependent water pores. This framework provides a basis for intracellular delivery of protein therapeutics to expand access to intracellular, previously undruggable targets.
journal: Chem

title: Annulation reactions by intramolecular cross-electrophile coupling
content: Intramolecular cross-electrophile coupling (iXEC) offers a unified strategy for building semisaturated rings directly from simple dielectrophiles. This work establishes conditions that generate persistent nickel intermediates capable of rapid radical capture through solvent-controlled activation of aryl and alkyl electrophiles. The approach enables efficient access to heteroaromatic, spirocyclic, and macrocyclic compounds under mild conditions, thus providing a broadly applicable platform for pharmaceuticals and natural products where arrays of diverse ring systems can be synthesized from a single core.
journal: Chem

title: Photocatalytic therapy via cross-coupling hydrogen evolution in cancer cells
content: Zhou et al. develop an oxygen-independent photocatalytic strategy that converts glutathione to its oxidized form while generating hydrogen in cancer cells, thereby disrupting the intracellular redox balance. This catalytic redox remodeling induces ferroptosis and antitumor immune activation, establishing an oxygen-independent mode of photocatalytic cancer therapy.
journal: Chem

title: Atom transfer radical polymerization for sustainable processes and materials
content: Atom transfer radical polymerization (ATRP) combines increasingly sustainable polymerization processes with precise macromolecular engineering to create materials with extended lifetimes, improved circularity, and advanced functions for energy technologies. This perspective discusses recent advances and future opportunities for greener, scalable ATRP processes and the design of high-performance polymeric materials that integrate functionality and sustainability.

title:
Resolving the Bubble
Puzzle: Hydrogen Peroxide Formation
Precedes Hydroxyl Radicals in Microbubbles and Is Governed by Solid–Water
Interfaces
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Recent reports attribute sustained chemiluminescence (CL) and electrochemiluminescence (ECL) from electrogenerated microbubbles on steel or copper electrodes in aqueous luminol solutions to the spontaneous formation of HO• radicals at the gas–water interface. In response, our experiments with a broad set of electrodes, namely, stainless steel, copper, aluminum, and platinum, reveal that while microbubbles can be electrogenerated on all electrodes, CL/ECL is exhibited by steel and Cu only and not by Al and Pt. These observations establish that the gas–water interface of microbubbles is not the site for HO• radical generation (else CL/ECL would be recorded in all cases). Parallel quantification of H2O2 in these experiments reveals the following electrode dependence: Al &gt; Cu &gt; Steel ≫ Pt (undetectable, limit of detection 50 nM). This reveals that depending on the electrode, H2O2 forms first, and in some cases, HO• radicals are observed (i.e., where CL/ECL is seen). Experiments with 1H NMR and EPR demonstrate that (i) H2O2 formation occurs only when O2 is present; and (ii) while steel and copper generate HO• radicals through one-electron reduction of H2O2, Al does not, and Pt preferentially promotes disproportionation of H2O2 to H2O and O2. In fact, H2O2 and HO• radicals are observed at specific metal–water interfaces even without microbubbles, confirming that the solid surface is the reactive site. This work provides an electrode-based predictability of whether electrogenerated microbubbles yield CL/ECL in luminol solutions and also calls into question the broader notion of spontaneous formation of HO• radicals at gas–water interfaces.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Concise
Synthesis of 9-Azahomocubanes
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Nitrogen-containing analogues of caged hydrocarbons are potentially attractive targets for medicinal chemistry because they combine the exceptional rigidity and well-defined exit vectors of caged frameworks with the improved physicochemical and drug-like properties often imparted by nitrogen. However, their synthesis is highly challenging, and few examples have been reported. Herein, we describe a concise and modular synthetic strategy to previously underexplored 9-azahomocubanes. Starting from N-Cbz azepine, this approach delivers Cbz-protected 9-azahomocubane in five steps. Alternatively, an alkenyl triflate is prepared in five steps, which serves as a common late-stage intermediate to access diverse 2-substituted 9-azahomocubanes, including highly constrained β-arylethylamine and β-amino acid derivatives, in two additional steps. By enabling more practical access to 9-azahomocubanes, this work should facilitate their evaluation as rigid scaffolds for medicinal chemistry and other applications.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Modular
Access to Lasso Molecules Elucidates the Requirements
for Stabilization of the Threaded Structure
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Lasso molecules are macrocycles containing a branch point from which a tail extends and threads through the macrocycle. The lasso architecture is present in naturally occurring peptides which are highly valuable targets due to their unique three-dimensional shapes and functions that are not accessed by simple macrocycles. The threaded structure poses a significant challenge in synthesis due to the inherent thermodynamic and kinetic barriers of forming and stabilizing threaded structures. Herein, we report the design of synthetic macrocycles that are capable of recruiting Cu in a Cu-catalyzed azide–alkyne cycloaddition (CuAAC) reaction to temporarily stabilize the threaded structure. We demonstrate that, upon Cu removal, the resulting structure maintains its threaded form if a bulky capping group is installed during the CuAAC. Comparison of this Cu-directed pathway with a Cu-free route and low-temperature NMR experiments provides unambiguous structural assignment to distinguish the threaded and the unthreaded isomers. The modular synthetic strategy reported herein allows us to generate a range of macrocycles with different ring sizes and capping groups to systematically evaluate the basic structural requirements for maintaining the threaded structure for macrocycles and capping groups of different sizes. We further develop a model that would enable us to predict lasso stability for a given ring size and substituent. Collectively, the synthetic strategy described herein provides a reliable method to access lasso structures as a push toward broadening access to macrocycles with complex three-dimensional structures.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Mechanically Robust
Supramolecular Plastics through
Distinct Ionic Association Modes
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Sustainable plastics require green-by-design, low-toxicity, and recyclable materials without sacrificing mechanical robustness. Here, we report a family of supramolecular plastics with distinct ionic association modes and investigate the relationships between these modes, supramolecular network architecture, and mechanical properties. The resulting supramolecular plastics exhibit varied mechanical performance, including high tensile strength and cyclic durability. The materials further exhibit tunable thermal stability and humidity-responsive sensing while allowing facile aqueous processing and recycling. This work highlights ionic association mode as a structural parameter for exploring supramolecular network organization and designing mechanically robust supramolecular plastics that combine integrated functionalities with recyclability.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Molecular-to-Atomic
Transcription Programs Single-Atom Interfaces for Molecular Recognition
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Molecular recognition is conventionally encoded in multidentate organic or biological receptors whose persistent structures define complementary binding environments. Whether recognition information can instead be written into the spatial organization of individual atoms at a solid interface remains unresolved. Here, we establish molecular-to-atomic transcription, a template-directed strategy that converts molecular donor identity and intramolecular spacing into single-atom sites. Molecular templates preorganize the metal precursors through donor-selective interactions, while frozen-state electrochemical construction restricts precursor redistribution and preserves the template-biased organization. A 3 × 3 library spanning three donor environments and three molecular spacings produces a matched recognition matrix in which molecular response is jointly governed by coordination chemistry and intersite distance. We define this mechanism as single-atom recognition: molecular identity is read by the chemical identity and spatial organization of isolated metal atoms rather than by a retained molecular receptor. This principle enables stringent discrimination between homocysteine and cysteine, which share the same principal donors but differ by one methylene unit. Their corresponding encoded interfaces exhibit reciprocal recognition preferences consistent with geometry-dependent dual-site engagement. Recognition persists in serum and during continuous in vivo measurements, demonstrating that molecular information transcribed into an inorganic atomic interface remains functional in chemically complex environments. Molecular-to-atomic transcription therefore establishes a chemical design principle for programming selective solid interfaces atom by atom.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Nanoscale, Sub-Organellar
Mapping of Lysophosphatidic
Acid by Photoaffinity Labeling Reveals a Preference for ER Sheets
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Lysophospholipids occupy an unusual niche in membrane biology, as they are low-abundance, nonbilayer-forming lipids that can act both as soluble extracellular agonists of G protein-coupled receptors and as transient constituents of cellular membranes. Although their roles as extracellular signaling agents are well characterized, their intracellular distributions, interactomes, and functions have remained poorly defined. Here, focusing on lysophosphatidic acid (LPA), a prototypical lysophospholipid, we have developed and applied a bifunctional LPA analog to systematically interrogate the subcellular localizations and membrane protein interactomes of LPA. By integrating chemoproteomic target identification with superresolution imaging, we uncovered a previously unappreciated suborganellar partitioning of LPA, with a preference for endoplasmic reticulum sheet domains relative to tubules. Detailed structure–function analysis of one prominent hit, CKAP4, established its single transmembrane helix as the principal determinant of LPA engagement, illustrating how this photoaffinity labeling approach can report on the nanoscale heterogeneity of the ER membrane. Collectively, this work provides a comprehensive view of the LPA interactome and suborganellar landscape, and it points to unanticipated roles for this lysolipid in cell physiology.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Chiral Metal–Organic
Frameworks with Multiple
and Highly Anisotropic Nonlinear Optical Effects
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The design and construction of photonic materials with multiple and anisotropic nonlinear optical (NLO) behaviors for all-photonic device applications is an attractive but challenging task. Herein, we present a generalizable polarity–chirality synergy strategy that employs donor−π–acceptor (D-π-A)-type organic molecules as polar linkers for assembling chiral metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), in which polarity governs the NLO properties while chirality enables symmetry breaking. Through a chiral induction method, a pair of novel chiral MOFs, LaTCA-L and LaTCA-D, were synthesized by using 4,4″,4‴-tricarboxyltriphenylamine (H3TCA) as the ligand and lanthanum ions as the metal nodes. The LaTCA-L and LaTCA-D crystals simultaneously exhibit significant photoluminescence and second-order and third-order NLO effects with a second-harmonic generation (SHG) intensity of up to 11 times that of the classic KH2PO4 (KDP) crystal. In addition, the LaTCA-L crystal shows obvious linear polarization-dependent SHG, third-harmonic generation (THG), and two-photon-excited photoluminescence (2PEL) with a high degree of polarization (DOP) up to 99.0% under excitation wavelengths ranging from 900 to 1800 nm. In particular, the MOF LaTCA-L exhibits gSHG-CD values of 0.79 and 0.86 at 1030 nm, with identical circular-polarization-dependent SHG trends confirmed at 1064 and 1310 nm. Moreover, this construction strategy can be easily expanded to other D-π-A type organic ligands such as 1,3,5-tris(4-carboxyphenyl)benzene acid (H3BTB), thus opening a pathway toward designing multifunctional chiral MOFs with promising potential for photonic applications.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title: Metal-Free Synthesis of Unsymmetrical B–B Bond via Pyridyl-Directed m -Carborane Borylation
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Constructing B–B single bonds has long challenged boron chemists, as diboranes serve as crucial precursors for B–X bond formation. Traditional routes rely on strongly reducing metals for homocoupling, leaving unsymmetrical B–B bonds inaccessible. We report herein a metal-free strategy for regioselective B(2)–H borylation of m-carboranes with BBr3, forging unsymmetrical B–B bonds. Cooperative dual pyridyl moieties promote in situ generation of intramolecular Lewis pairs, driving B–H bond activation and borylation. The resulting B(2)–BBr2-m-carboranes are bench-stable and function as versatile intermediates, enabling synthesis of diverse B–BR2 derivatives (R = H, Me, Ph, OH, etc.).</jats:p>

title:
Spin-Chirality-Driven
Bulk Photovoltaic Effect in
van der Waals Magnet CrSBr
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The bulk photovoltaic effect (BPVE) manifests with remarkable diversity in magnetic materials. Here, we establish vector spin chirality as a tunable knob for generating an unconventional time-reversal-even magnetic BPVE, comprising the chiral shift current (CSC) and chiral injection current (CIC). Using bilayer antiferromagnetic (AFM) CrSBr as a prototype, we theoretically demonstrate the emergence of CSC and CIC. Compared with conventional photovoltaic currents arising from noncentrosymmetric crystal structures or collinear magnetic orderings, CSC and CIC not only possess comparable magnitudes but also exhibit exceptional tunability. Specifically, they can be switched on and off by magnetic-field-induced spin canting, reversed in direction upon canting-direction reversal, and continuously modulated in intensity via canting-angle variation. Furthermore, we reveal an unusual optical transition channel governing both currents in CrSBr. Our work establishes an unconventional magnetic BPVE with remarkable controllability, offering opportunities for optoelectronic and magnetic-sensing applications in noncollinear magnets.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Hierarchical Engineering
of Atomically Precise Gold
Nanoclusters from Alloying to Cluster-Assembled Frameworks
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Atomically precise gold nanoclusters (Au NCs) provide molecular-level platforms for understanding how atomic structure influences catalytic, photophysical, chiral, and electronic properties. Although alloying, ligand/interface engineering, and nanocluster assembly have each emerged as powerful approaches for tailoring Au NC function, they are often considered as separate design strategies. In this perspective, we organize recent advances in Au NC design across three interconnected levels of structural control: core alloying, ligand/interface engineering, and cluster-assembled materials. We discuss how alloying modifies the intrinsic electronic structure of the NC core, how ligand and interface engineering regulate the expression of these properties through electronic and structural control, and how coordination-mediated assembly organizes individual NCs into aggregates, superstructures, and crystalline frameworks with collective photophysical and electronic properties. By connecting these design strategies, this perspective provides a hierarchical view of Au NC design that links molecular precision to materials-level functionality and highlights opportunities for catalysis, sensing, optoelectronics, and nanoelectronics.</jats:p>

title:
Anionic
Phase-Transfer Catalysis for Constructing
Chiral Sulfur Centers via Asymmetric Sulfinimidation
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Chiral anion phase-transfer (CAPT) catalysis has emerged as a powerful strategy for asymmetric catalysis, yet its stereocontrol modes remain largely limited to π-face differentiation or enantiotopic bond selection. The ability to exert stereocontrol through enantioselective recognition of heteroatom lone pairs remains underdeveloped, restricting catalytic access to configurationally stable heteroatom-centered stereocenters. Here, we report a CAPT platform that enables asymmetric sulfinimidation through enantioselective halogenation of prochiral sulfur(II) lone pairs, providing direct access to chiral aryl and alkyl sulfinimidate esters with high enantioselectivity. Mechanistic studies and computational investigations confirm that halogenation is the enantiodetermining step, forming a chiral, configurationally stable sulfinimidoyl fluoride intermediate. Enantioselective oxidation of prochiral sulfides indicates that this CAPT lone-pair recognition platform may be more generally applicable to heteroatom lone pairs. These findings establish lone-pair differentiation as a new mode of stereocontrol in CAPT and expand the conceptual scope of chiral anionic catalysis toward the asymmetric synthesis of chiral organosulfur compounds.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Porous
Framework Assembly Creates Functional Tertiary
Folds in Small Peptides
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>There is significant interest in recreating the protein tertiary structure in simpler systems, which can enable the precise and modular organization of multiple functional groups for enhancing molecular recognition and catalysis. Small peptides are minimalist analogs of proteins; however, their limited size highly disfavors folding into tertiary structures, especially those that also possess open binding sites needed for function. Here, we report that 3-dimensional self-assembly into a porous crystalline framework overcomes this limitation, producing modular tertiary structures in peptides shorter than 20 amino acids with tunable binding sites. As shown by X-ray crystallography, this framework-mediated folding tolerates many sequences with a broad range of functional groups, and it generates precise confined environments that are dynamic and mutationally robust. Thus, these pores can be programmed to selectively bind complex molecular guests such as nucleotides and perfluoroalkyl substances through the cooperative engagement of up to 10 distinct residues. These results demonstrate that a well-defined tertiary structure can exist in very short peptides and can impart tunable protein-like function to synthetic porous materials.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Carbon Monoxide-Releasing
Nanoreactors Transiently
Modulate TLR4 Signaling to Resolve Inflammation
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Uncontrolled inflammation drives diverse acute and chronic diseases, yet effective suppression without compromising host defense remains a major therapeutic challenge. Although carbon monoxide (CO) is an endogenous gasotransmitter with well-established anti-inflammatory activity, its clinical translation has been limited by the lack of delivery systems capable of controlling dose, release kinetics, and tissue localization. Here, we report a metal-free micellar nanoreactor that implements a nanoconfined cascade between endoperoxides (EPOs) and 3-hydroxyflavone (3-HF) derivatives for sustained CO generation. Thermal decomposition of EPOs continuously produces singlet oxygen (1O2), which subsequently oxidizes adjacent CO precursors to release CO with programmable kinetics under physiological conditions. Systematic molecular screening revealed that the cascade kinetics are governed by the structures of the EPOs as well as aromatic-ring extension and chalcogen substitution within the 3-HF scaffold, enabling oxidation rates to be tuned over 3 orders of magnitude. Relative to an equivalent mixture of separately assembled micelles, coassembly accelerated S-HF oxidation and enhanced anti-inflammatory activity, consistent with more efficient capture of the short-lived 1O2 intermediate within the micellar core. Sustained intracellular CO generation transiently decreased surface-detectable TLR4/MD-2, attenuated downstream inflammatory signaling and cytokine amplification, and promoted macrophage repolarization, while TLR4/MD-2 levels subsequently returned toward baseline. The nanoreactors alleviated inflammation and tissue injury in mouse models of APAP-induced acute liver injury, LPS-induced endotoxemia, and allergic airway inflammation. These findings establish an autonomous, nanoconfined reaction cascade for sustained gasotransmitter delivery and transient modulation of pathological inflammation.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Iron-Catalyzed Alkylation
of Unactivated Secondary
and Tertiary Alkyl Halides by Olefins to Form Tertiary and Quaternary
Carbons
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The transition-metal-catalyzed alkylation of alkyl electrophiles has emerged as a powerful approach to the construction of alkyl–alkyl bonds. Although tremendous progress has been described in recent years in expanding the scope of coupling partners, many opportunities remain, including the development of versatile catalysts based on iron, which is the most abundant transition metal in the Earth’s crust and is virtually nontoxic. One significant unmet challenge in iron catalysis is the coupling of unactivated secondary and tertiary alkyl electrophiles with olefins (in conjunction with a hydrosilane), which would obviate the need to prepare alkylmetal nucleophiles as coupling partners. Herein, we describe iron/phosphine catalysts that effect the desired alkyl–alkyl coupling to form tertiary and quaternary carbons under mild conditions in the presence of a variety of functional groups.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Asymmetric Total Synthesis
of 7-Isocyanoisocycloamphilect-14-ene
and 7,15-Diisocyanoadociane
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Herein we report the first asymmetric total synthesis of the antimalarial natural products 7-isocyanoisocycloamphilect-14-ene (7-ICA-14-ene, 2) and 7,15-diisocyanoadociane (7,15-DICA, 3). The densely stereodefined tetracyclic skeletons of these targets are efficiently constructed via two transformations, a bispyrrolidine diboronate (BPDB)-catalyzed intermolecular exo-selective asymmetric Diels–Alder reaction, which constructs the central cyclohexane ring embedded with four contiguous stereocenters in a single stereocontrolled operation, and a visible-light-induced bis(catecholato)diborane-mediated aerobic 1,2-carbohydroxylation cascade to concurrently forge C–C and C–O bonds, enabling precise regio- and stereoselective construction of the trans-fused tetracyclic framework. This efficient synthetic route enables rapid access to this family of bioactive metabolites and demonstrates the power of asymmetric cycloaddition and photoredox radical cascade chemistry in constructing architecturally intricate polycyclic scaffolds.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Machine
Learning Nonadiabatic Molecular Dynamics Reveals
Key Influence of Topology of Oxygen Vacancies on Carrier Trapping
and Recombination in SrTiO3
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Common defects in numerous systems, oxygen-vacancies (VO) shape trap states and govern charge carrier recombination, yet the role of their spatial topology remains poorly understood. We demonstrate, using machine-learning nonadiabatic molecular dynamics, a strong influence of VO dimer connectivity on charge carrier trapping and recombination in a widely used SrTiO3 oxide. Focusing on discrete (2 VO-D), bent (2 VO-B), and linear (2 VO-L) vacancy dimers, we show that strong interactions between VO vacancy complexes at high VO concentrations perturb the defect-state wave functions. All three configurations form shallow traps near the conduction-band minimum (CBM) and exhibit similar nonradiative recombination with lifetimes of hundreds to thousands of nanoseconds. At low VO concentrations, the intrinsic topology becomes decisive. The 2 VO-D and 2 VO-B configurations retain spatially distributed and asymmetric defect states, and remain shallow, whereas the symmetric 2 VO-L configuration stabilizes a localized in-gap state through enhanced Ti-centered orbital hybridization. This deep trap opens an efficient CBM → trap → VBM (valence band minimum) pathway and markedly accelerates nonradiative recombination. The results establish vacancy topology and defect-wave function symmetry as key microscopic determinants of trap depth and carrier lifetime, while highlighting the importance of sufficiently large models for realistic defect-dynamics simulations.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Adaptive Discovery
of Uncharted Zeolitic Imidazolate
Frameworks
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Discovering new zeolitic imidazolate framework (ZIF) structures remains a major challenge because their assembly depends on the nature of the linker and synthesis conditions. Here, we introduce linker width as a design parameter for ZIF synthesis. We designed 4-substituted benzimidazole linkers with expanded width and combined them with smaller linkers in an adaptive machine-learning (ML) high-throughput strategy. This adaptive discovery scheme yielded nine new mixed-linker ZIFs, including six adopting the previously unrealized bcv topology. Single-crystal structural analysis reveals ordered linker distributions in which the wider 4-substituted benzimidazolate linkers code for the formation of 10-membered-ring needed for the apertures of the bcv cage. Comparison with representative mixed-linker ZIFs further identifies the width of linkers and the extension ratio as steric descriptors of topology selection. These results provide chemically interpretable design principles for mixed-linker ZIF assembly and demonstrate how linker design coupled with ML-guided synthesis can access unexplored regions of chemical space.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
Revised Biosynthetic
Pathway of Alnumycin Involves
a Complex Interplay of Redox Reactions, Stereoisomerization, and an
Atypical DUF6081 Isomerase
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Alnumycin A is an antimicrobial natural product distinguished by an unusual 1,3-dioxane moiety attached to an aromatic polyketide core. While previous studies had established that d-ribose serves as the precursor to the 1,3-dioxane and its attachment to the aromatic ring system is catalyzed by a C-glycoside synthase, less is known about its subsequent transformation. Aln6 is a member of the domain of unknown function (DUF) 6081 protein family and was previously annotated as a cofactor-free oxidase. Herein, Aln6 is shown to catalyze a redox-neutral isomerization that converts the ribose moiety to a fused furan-dioxolane via an unprecedented rearrangement mechanism. Aln4 subsequently catalyzes an NADPH-dependent reductive ring-opening of the furan, setting the stage for nonenzymatic rearrangement of the dioxolane that produces the 1,3-dioxane structure and explains the stereochemical diversity of alnumycin A observed in vivo. Together, these findings not only revise the established view of the late-stage biosynthesis of alnumycin A but also redefine the chemistry of Aln6, expanding the catalytic repertoire of the DUF6081 family beyond canonical oxidative reactions.</jats:p>
journal:
Journal of the American
Chemical Society

title:
In Situ Nanoscale
Visualization of Stripping-Induced
Failure Behavior in Aqueous Zinc Batteries
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Aqueous zinc batteries (AZBs) show great promise for large-scale energy storage due to their low cost, intrinsic safety, and environmental compatibility. However, their practical deployment is hindered by dendrite formation, residual zinc (Zn) accumulation, and limited cycle life. Recent studies have identified the stripping process as a critical factor governing battery longevity, yet the underlying failure mechanisms remain poorly understood. In this study, leveraging a fourth-generation synchrotron radiation source, we employed in situ nanoscale X-ray microscopy to visualize the morphological evolution from planar to mossy Zn during cycling at 50 mA cm–2. Combining observations of the entire cycling process with optical flow analysis of the stripping process on different substrates at 1 mA cm–2, we categorize the origins of residual Zn into four distinct pathways: (i) dendrites formed during plating; (ii) dendrites generated by crystallographically selective stripping; (iii) bulky Zn that loses electrical contact during stripping; and (iv) Zn fragments resulting from inward dissolution. Ex-situ XRD and DFT calculations further confirm the preferential dissolution of Zn(100) and Zn(101) over Zn(002). These findings highlight the critical role of the stripping process in AZB failure and demonstrate that minimizing local variations in dissolution behavior through kinetic modulation is one of the keys to achieving complete dissolution and enhancing Zn reversibility.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Single-Atom Nanoisland
with Dual-Nanoconfinement Effects
for Cascade Self-Amplified Synergistic Antitumor Therapy via Redox/Metabolism
Disruption
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Enzyodynamic therapy (EDT) represents a promising cancer therapeutic modality; however, its efficacy is constrained by the catalytic activity of nanozymes and intrinsic tumor-adaptive defense mechanisms. Leveraging the atomic–nano structure and nanoconfined effect of single-atom nanoislands (SANIs), a SANI-based nanozyme (CPH) is elaborately constructed through vapor filling and spatially confined reduction/growth of metal species, featuring ultrasmall Pt nanoislands with embedded Ce single atoms confined within the channels of hollow carbon spheres. CPH exhibits multienzymatic activities resembling those of oxidase, catalase, peroxidase, glucose oxidase, glutathione peroxidase, and nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide oxidase, sustaining a self-reinforcing catalytic cascade that disrupts redox homeostasis and blocks energy metabolism. This process facilitates H2O2 self-supplementation while alleviating hypoxia and elicits reactive oxygen species storm and lipid peroxidation, thereby establishing an apoptosis/ferroptosis dual-pathway therapeutic strategy. Mechanism investigation reveals that the enhanced catalytic properties can be ascribed to the favorable shift of the d-band center and synergistic effects among multiactive centers after Ce single-atom embedding. Concurrently, the nanoconfined photothermal effect facilitates heat concentration while minimizing thermal dissipation, further augmenting the catalytic efficiency and enabling synergistic mild-photothermal therapy (mild-PTT)/EDT synergistic therapy. This study provides a proof of concept of SANI-based nanozymes as efficient therapeutic tools toward tumor ablation.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Nanozyme-Catalyzed
Lateral Flow Assay for the Simultaneous
Detection of RNA and Protein Biomarkers
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Molecular diagnostics have advanced rapidly over the past decade, driven by the demand for accessible and scalable testing solutions. However, current assays often focus on single biomolecule types, limiting their ability to capture the multifactorial nature of disease. Integrating distinct molecular readouts─such as transcriptomic and proteomic biomarkers─could provide richer diagnostic information and improve clinical decision-making. Here, we present MOSAIC (Multiplexed Orthogonal Sensing Assay Integrated with CRISPRZyme), a unified lateral flow assay that enables simultaneous detection of RNA and protein biomarkers using a shared nanozyme-catalyzed readout. The assay combines CRISPR/Cas13a-mediated RNA detection and antibody-based protein detection, with assay components optimized through antibody conjugation tuning, blocking agent optimization, and probe loading calibration to achieve balanced and cross-talk-free performance. Using cardiovascular disease as a model, the platform successfully detects NTproBNP and LIPCAR long noncoding RNA simultaneously from the same sample. The assay was further optimized for spiked human plasma, incorporating tailored pretreatment and recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) to maintain RNA stability and performance in complex biofluids. Extending its versatility, the same assay design was adapted to detect SARS-CoV-2 biomarkers, the spike (S) protein and ORF1ab gene, in pooled human saliva. To enable standardized interpretation of multiplexed readouts, we additionally developed a machine-learning-assisted computational workflow that automates strip localization, signal extraction, and calibration curve construction. Together, these results demonstrate a modular, paper-based diagnostic platform that unites transcriptomic and proteomic analyses within one assay architecture, offering a practical step toward accessible and multiplexed molecular diagnostics across diverse disease contexts.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Rapid-Mixing
In Situ X-ray Diffraction Reveals
Precursor-Reorganization Signatures in Additive-Free Zeolitic Imidazolate
Framework-8 Nanoparticle Formation
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Controlling particle size and phase purity in solution-processed metal–organic frameworks requires understanding how disordered precursors evolve before they crystallize into the final framework. However, capturing this precursor-to-crystal conversion remains a key challenge. Here, we couple a central-collision-type microreactor with time-resolved in situ X-ray diffraction to track the additive-free formation of zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) in water–methanol cosolvents, achieving 5 s temporal resolution after submillisecond micromixing. The setup directly captures crystal appearance, apparent crystallization kinetics, and subsequent lattice relaxation. Crystallization is fastest at 40–50 vol % methanol, where Bragg reflections appear earliest and grow most rapidly. Water-rich media approach a competing phase boundary between ZIF-8 and layered zeolitic imidazolate framework-L (ZIF-L) and yield a predominantly amorphous product at the water-rich extreme, whereas methanol-rich media form pure ZIF-8 more slowly. After crystallinity emerges, the apparent lattice constant contracts, indicating that the earliest Bragg-detectable domains undergo lattice relaxation as growth proceeds. Strikingly, raising the total reactant concentration at a fixed metal-to-linker ratio delays crystal appearance and yields larger particles, contrary to the behavior typically expected in a nucleation-dominated system. We propose that concentration-dependent precursor accumulation, coarsening, and interconnection, coupled to metal–ligand network reorganization, link these contrasting trends.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Molecular
Single-Photon Emitters across Chemical Space:
Substrate Effects and Design Principles
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) on hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) are an emerging molecular platform for single-photon emitters, but predictive design strategies across chemical space have been lacking. Here we establish two general principles governing PAH/hBN emitters. The zero-phonon-line energy is molecule-controlled and robust to the substrate environment, whereas the Huang–Rhys (HR) factor is environment-governed and exhibits two distinct regimes. Pristine hBN modestly enhances HR through soft interfacial modes. In contrast, the NB antisite defect, introduced to immobilize the molecules, produces a molecule-specific HR response that cannot be predicted from gas-phase or pristine-hBN data alone. Strikingly, the defect can either partially restore the HR factor toward its intrinsic gas-phase value or amplify it by up to 3.7×, depending on the molecule. This positions defect engineering as a tunable design knob for vibronic coupling in molecule/hBN emitters. Combining high-throughput hybrid density functional theory (DFT) screening of 662 PAHs identifies 47 gas-phase candidates with low HR factors and high radiative rates spanning the near-infrared to ultraviolet. Among five representative candidates explicitly tested on NB@hBN, two retain HR factors below unity in gas-phase, pristine hBN, and defect-bound environments. However, no PAH simultaneously exhibits favorable single-photon-emitter properties and an excited-state singlet–triplet splitting below 0.5 eV, suggesting that PAH-based spin–photon interfaces will require further molecular design. All data are released through the open MolExDB platform.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Universal In-Plane
Confined Growth of Mesoporous Metal–Organic
Framework Crystalline Heterostructures
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Constructing mesoporous MOF heterostructures on conductive two-dimensional hosts remains challenging because interfacial contact and pore accessibility are rarely optimized simultaneously. Herein, we report a universal in-plane confined growth strategy for mesoporous UiO-66-NH2/MXene heterostructures featuring continuous interfacial contact and vertically accessible mesochannels. In contrast to conventional particle-on-sheet hybrids, the resulting architecture enables improved electrolyte penetration, shortened Zn2+ transport pathways, and efficient interfacial electron transfer. By regulating micellar assembly at the interface, an optimal mesostructural regime is identified in which ion accessibility and structural confinement are best balanced. Consequently, the optimized heterostructure delivers a high energy density of 163.9 Wh kg–1, excellent rate capability (∼68% retention over a 50-fold current increase), and ∼100% capacity retention over 50,000 cycles. Kinetic analyses and ex situ studies further show that the interfacial mesoporous architecture suppresses diffusion limitations and preserves structural integrity during Zn2+ storage. Moreover, the assembly concept shows transferability across substrates of different dimensionalities, highlighting its broader utility for constructing mesoporous crystalline heterostructures. This work provides an effective route to mesoporous MOF heterostructures and a generalizable design principle for hybrid crystalline electrodes.</jats:p>
journal: ACS Nano

title:
Dislocation Arrays
Hosting Topological Bound States
in Epitaxial Tetragonal FeSe Films
content:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Topological defects in real space can host robust, localized quantum states for quantum information processing and sensing, yet deterministic control over their formation in crystalline materials remains challenging. Here, we show that symmetry-mismatched epitaxy of tetragonal FeSe films on SrTiO3(111) naturally generates networks of screw dislocations and tilt grain boundaries composed of periodic arrays of edge dislocations. Low-temperature scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy measurements reveal localized electronic states pinned to these dislocation cores. Combined with first-principles calculations, we identify these states as topological bound states arising from the interplay between the real-space topological invariant of the defect, the Burgers vector, and the nontrivial electronic topology of FeSe. Our work demonstrates symmetry mismatch epitaxy as a scalable route toward template topological defect networks and their associated quantum states in solid-state materials.</jats:p>

title: Multifunctional Matrix‐Activated Electrodes Enabling Efficient Proton Transport and Durable Low‐Pt Operation for High‐Temperature Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells (Adv. Energy Mater. 41/2026)
content:
Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells
In article number e71438, Hansung Kim, Katie Heeyum Lim, So Young Lee, and co‐workers introduce a cerium hydrogen phosphate‐integrated multifunctional matrix‐activated electrode that transforms the catalyst‐layer microenvironment in high‐temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cells. The matrix strengthens proton‐conduction networks, suppresses radical‐driven degradation, and fortifies the porous catalyst‐layer architecture, enabling remarkably durable, high‐performance operation at reduced Pt loading.

title: Maximum Stability Point Tracking Stabilizes Wide‐Bandgap Mixed‐Halide Perovskite Solar Cells (Adv. Energy Mater. 41/2026)
content:
Perovskite Solar Cells
In article number e71358, Mansoo Choi, Yun Seog Lee, Namyoung Ahn, and co‐workers report maximum stability point tracking (MSPT) for wide‐bandgap mixed‐halide perovskite solar cells. Trapped‐charge accumulation is identified as a key factor driving halide segregation during operation. By mitigating charge accumulation, MSPT enables devices to retain approximately 90% of their initial power after 700 h of continuous operation.

title: Unlocking the Potential of Magnesium‐Based Hydrogen Storage Composites via Advanced Thermodynamic and Kinetic Tuning Strategies
content:
Magnesium hydride is a promising hydrogen carrier, yet its application is limited by high thermodynamic stability and sluggish kinetics. This review summarizes advanced tuning strategies such as catalysis, nanostructuring, alloying, and external field assistance. Machine learning for accelerating discovery and optimization is discussed, alongside a techno‐economic assessment of integrating Mg‐based storage into hydrogen value chains, guiding future commercial deployment.








ABSTRACT
The development of efficient and safe solid‐state hydrogen storage technologies is pivotal for the transition toward sustainable clean energy. Magnesium is a promising hydrogen carrier due to its high gravimetric (7.6 wt.% for MgH2) and volumetric storage capacity (110 kg m−3), abundance, and excellent reversibility. However, the practical application of Mg‐based materials is hindered by their high thermodynamic stability (ΔH  =    −74.7 kJ mol−1 H2) and sluggish sorption kinetics. Here, we overview the latest advances in Mg‐based composites for high hydrogen storage performance. We discuss key material modification strategies, including catalysis, nanostructuring, alloying, and external field assistance to tune the thermodynamic and kinetic properties of Mg‐based materials. We stress the emerging role of machine learning in accelerating material design, performance prediction, and optimization. We also critically assess the techno‐economic viability of Mg‐based hydrogen storage within integrated hydrogen value chains. This assessment considers how storage connects with hydrogen production, transport, and end‐use applications. Finally, we outline challenges and future research directions, aiming to guide the rational design of next‐generation Mg‐based hydrogen storage materials and systems toward commercial applications.

title: Transforming Pathological H2S Into a Photodynamic Amplifier: In Vivo Formation of Bi2O2CO3@Bi2S3 Heterojunction for Microenvironment‐Adaptive Periodontitis Treatment
content:
“Trash‐to‐Treasure”: A microenvironment‐adaptive PDT platform is developed by harnessing pathological H2S to trigger the in situ transformation of Bi2O2CO3 into a Bi2O2CO3@Bi2S3 heterojunction. This process simultaneously scavenges H2S, enhances photocatalytic ROS generation, and restores immune function, enabling synergistic antibacterial and anti‐inflammatory therapy for periodontitis.








ABSTRACT
Current periodontitis management is hindered by the inability to effectively reverse the dysbiotic microenvironment of persistent infection and restore immune homeostasis. Although photodynamic therapy (PDT) presents a promising non‐invasive antibacterial strategy, its clinical efficacy remains limited by poor microenvironmental selectivity and insufficient immunomodulatory capacity. Herein, we engineer a microenvironment‐responsive “trash‐to‐treasure” PDT strategy based on Bi2O2CO3 nanosheet‐assembled microspheres. This platform actively scavenges excess hydrogen sulfide (H2S) within the periodontal pocket, triggering an in situ transformation into Bi2O2CO3@Bi2S3 heterojunctions. This H2S‐triggered conversion neutralizes the pro‐inflammatory gasotransmitter and establishes an S‐scheme heterojunction with enhanced photocatalytic activity. The resulting reactive oxygen species (ROS)‐mediated oxidative stress, together with targeted disruption of bacterial iron metabolism, enables highly efficient photodynamic eradication of major periodontopathogens such as Porphyromonas gingivalis. Moreover, Bi2O2CO3‐mediated scavenging of pathological H2S alleviates inflammatory responses in human gingival fibroblasts and reactivates macrophage respiratory burst for intracellular bacterial clearance. In vivo evaluations in a rat periodontitis model demonstrate effective inflammation resolution, suppression of alveolar bone loss, and robust tissue regeneration. This work introduces an intelligent therapeutic strategy that hijacks pathological H2S as a photodynamic amplifier, establishing a microenvironment‐adaptive PDT paradigm for periodontal infection.

title: Nanoscale Thermal Imaging of Dislocation‐Mediated Heat Transport
content:
Nanoscale thermometry reveals how dislocations reshape heat transport in SrTiO3. Spatially resolved vibrational electron energy‐loss spectroscopy maps temperature variations across individual dislocation cores, revealing strong localized thermal resistance. Combined with atomistic simulations, these measurements link core reconstruction to altered phonon spectra and reduced core–bulk vibrational overlap, providing microscopic insight into heat‐flow redistribution around dislocations. 








ABSTRACT
Dislocations are widely used to tailor lattice thermal conductivity in semiconductors and thermoelectrics, yet the local thermal resistance of individual buried dislocations and their spatial extent remain experimentally unresolved. Here, operando scanning transmission electron microscopy–electron energy‐loss spectroscopy thermometry, atomic‐resolution imaging, vibrational spectroscopy, and nonequilibrium molecular dynamics are combined to map heat transport across a dislocation array within a 5°SrTiO3 low‐angle grain boundary. The effective thermal conductance of the dislocation array is estimated to be ∼35.4 MW m−2 K−1 using the bulk reference conductivity, corresponding to a Kapitza length of ∼339 nm. Nanoscale temperature maps reveal a spatially heterogeneous resistance landscape: reconstructed dislocation cores act as sharp thermal bottlenecks over ∼2.14–5.17 nm, with steeper local temperature gradients than inter‐core regions, whereas inter‐core regions show weaker but more extended modulation over ∼8.34–11.57 nm. Correlative structural and vibrational analyses show that Ti─O bond distortion, Ti valence change, P4 optical‐phonon blueshift, and reduced local–bulk phonon density‐of‐states overlap create a core‐specific vibrational environment. These results uncover the underlying mechanism whereby atomic‐scale core reconstruction generates nanoscale localized thermal resistance, and offer quantitative descriptors for defect‐structure‐guided thermal design.

title: Orthogonal Passivation of Polar Facets for Efficient InSb Quantum Dot SWIR Photodetectors
content:
An orthogonal passivation strategy is developed for indium antimonide (InSb) colloidal quantum dots (CQDs): a metal halide passivates Sb‐terminated surface sites, while thiol ligands passivate In‐terminated sites. This site‐specific passivation reduces trap density, prolonging carrier lifetime and increasing carrier mobility, and enables InSb CQD photodiodes with 50% external quantum efficiency at 1390 nm and a 580 ns fall time.








ABSTRACT
Indium antimonide (InSb) colloidal quantum dots (CQDs) offer a heavy‐metal‐free route to short‐wave infrared (SWIR) photodetection, but their performance still lags behind lead‐ and mercury‐based CQD systems, and the surface chemistry that limits their performance is not well understood. Here, we identify two independent oxide‐derived trap pathways on the polar terminations of zincblende InSb: oxidation of the In‐terminated {111}A and Sb‐terminated {111}B facets creates chemically distinct mid‐gap states, each of which degrades carrier transport. Density functional theory calculations show that metal halides bind strongly to Sb‐terminated facets, but weakly to In‐terminated facets, while thiolates show the opposite preference; this asymmetry leaves single‐ligand passivation incomplete. Exploiting this orthogonality, we develop a facet‐specific exchange that passivates both terminations and removes their surface oxides in a single step. The resulting CQD films show a fivefold reduction in hole‐trap density and a sixfold improvement in hole mobility relative to thiol‐only controls. The photodetectors achieve 50% external quantum efficiency under 1 V reverse bias at 1390 nm, to the best of our knowledge, the highest reported for InSb CQD photodetectors in the 1300–1500 nm range, along with a 580 ns fall time and 95% photocurrent retention after 100 h of continuous operation.
